Commentary of al-Tha'alabi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 25, verses 1–10:

Makkiyya (Meccan). It has three thousand, seven hundred and thirty-three letters, eight hundred and ninety-two words, and seventy-seven verses.

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Muqri informed us more than once, saying: Al-Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili and the memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu al-Shaykh Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani informed us, both saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Sharik told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus told us, saying: Sallam ibn Sulaym told us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir told us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Furqan will be raised on the Day of Resurrection believing that ﴿the Hour is surely coming, there is no doubt in it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves﴾, and he will enter Paradise without reckoning." [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 7/278.] [76]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Tabaraka﴾ is a form of tafa''ala, derived from al-barakah (blessing). According to Ibn Abbas, its meaning is as if it said: He has come with every blessing. Its evidence is the saying of al-Hasan: "Blessing comes from Him." Al-Dahhak said: "He is magnified." Al-Khalil said: "He is glorified." The root of barakah is growth and increase.

The scholars who verify (al-Muhaqqiqun) said: The meaning of this attribute is that it has been established and endures, by what has never ceased and will not cease. The root of barakah is firmness; it is said: "The bird settled (barraka) on the water," and "the camel knelt (barraka)." It is said: "Tabaraka Allah," and it is not said of Allah "mutabarik" or "mubarak," because His attributes and names are confined to where revelation has given authority (tawqif).

﴿Who has sent down the Criterion (al-Furqan)﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿upon His servant﴾, Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾, the jinn and mankind.

Some of them said: The warner is the Qur'an. It was said: It is Muhammad.

﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and He has not taken a son, and there is no partner for Him in dominion, and He created everything﴾ of what may be described as created, ﴿and determined it with precise determination﴾, meaning He shaped it and prepared it for what suits it, so there is no defect in it and no disproportion.

﴿Yet they have taken, besides Him, gods who create nothing, and they are themselves created, and they possess no power to harm or benefit themselves, and possess no power over death, nor life, nor resurrection﴾. These are the worshippers of idols. ﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾, meaning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and his companions: ﴿This is nothing but a falsehood which he has invented, and other people have helped him at it﴾, meaning the Jews, according to Mujahid. Al-Hasan ibn Ubayd ibn al-Hadr said: "The Abyssinian soothsayer." It was also said: Jabr, Yasar and Addas, the freedman of Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So they have brought injustice and falsehood﴾, meaning those who uttered this statement, by attributing the speech of Allah to fabrication and invention. ﴿And they said: "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ That is, they are read to him.

Then Allah the Exalted said, refuting them and denying them: ﴿Say: "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth; indeed He is ever Forgiving, Merciful."﴾ ﴿And they said: "What is with this Messenger that he eats food as we eat and walks in the markets"﴾, seeking livelihood, [In the second copy there is an addition: "as we walk."] ﴿"Why has an angel not been sent down to him to accompany him as a warner?"﴾, confirming him; ﴿"or a treasure be thrown to him, that he may spend from it, so that he need not busy himself with seeking livelihood"﴾; ﴿"or he have a garden from which he eats"﴾. This is the reading of the majority. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with a nun, meaning "we eat."

﴿And the wrongdoers said: "You follow only a man affected by sorcery."﴾ This verse was revealed concerning the story of Ibn Abi Umayya, and its mention has already passed in Bani Isra'il.

﴿Look, O Muhammad, how they have struck for you the examples, so they have strayed, and they cannot find a way﴾ to guidance or an escape from misguidance. Allah informs that they hold fast to ignorance and error, turning away from right guidance and correctness, while they were nonetheless obligated to accept the truth. Thus it is established that the capacity by which they stray is other than the capacity by which guidance and faith are attained.

﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that﴾, that is, than what they said, according to Mujahid. Ikrimah related from Ibn Abbas, who said: It means better than walking in the markets and seeking livelihood. Then He explained what that better thing is, saying the Exalted: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾, that is, lofty houses; it is called a palace (qasr) because it confines (qasara) and prevents access to it. The reciters differed concerning His saying ﴿and He will give﴾: Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir and Asim, through the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, read it with a raised final letter, while the others read it with a jussive, on the position of the conditional clause in His saying ﴿if He wills, He will give﴾.

[We were informed] [Not in the manuscript.] Abu Amr Ahmad ibn Abi Ahmad ibn Hamdun al-Nisaburi informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Bukhari informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd ibn Farwa al-Bukhari told us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa Ishaq ibn Bishr al-Bukhari told us, saying: Juwaybir told us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the polytheists reproached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with poverty, saying: ﴿What is with this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets?﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) grieved over that, and Gabriel descended to him from his Lord, consoling him, and said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. The Lord of Might sends you peace and says to you: ﴿We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾," and they seek livelihood in the world.

He said: While Gabriel (peace be upon him) and the Prophet (ﷺ) were conversing, Gabriel melted until he became like a hirda. It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is a hirda?" He said: "A lizard." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Gabriel, what is wrong with you, that you have melted until you became like a hirda?" He said: "O Muhammad, a door of the doors of heaven has been opened which had never been opened before, and the angel has been moved. If it is opened, it is either mercy or punishment, and I fear that your people will be punished for their reproach of you with poverty." The Prophet (ﷺ) and Gabriel (peace be upon him) then began to weep, when Gabriel returned and said: "O Muhammad, rejoice! This is Ridwan, the keeper of Paradise, who has come to you with the good pleasure of your Lord." Ridwan came and greeted him, then said: "O Muhammad, the Lord of Might sends you peace"—and with him was a casket of light, shining—"and your Lord says to you: These are the keys to the treasuries of the world, together with what will not be diminished for you of what is with Me in the Hereafter, equal to the wing of a mosquito." The Prophet (ﷺ) looked at Gabriel (peace be upon him) as one seeking his counsel, and Gabriel struck the earth with his hand and said: "Be humble before Allah." He said: "O Ridwan, I have no need of it. Poverty is more beloved to me, and that I be a patient, grateful servant." Ridwan said: "You are right; may Allah make you right."

A call came from heaven, and Gabriel raised his head, and behold, the heavens had opened their doors up to the Throne. Allah the Exalted revealed to the Garden of Eden that it should lower a branch of its boughs over him, upon which was a cluster, upon which was a bough of green chrysolite, with seventy thousand red rubies. Gabriel said: "O Muhammad, raise your gaze." He raised it and saw the dwellings and chambers of the prophets, and behold, his dwelling was above the dwellings of the prophets, a special excellence for him, and a caller called: "Are you pleased, O Muhammad?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am pleased. So make what you intended to give me in this world a treasure with You for intercession on the Day of Resurrection." [Asbab Nuzul al-Ayat, al-Wahidi al-Naysaburi: 225.] [77]

They narrate that this verse was revealed by Ridwan: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾.

Then Allah the Exalted said, refuting them and denying them: ﴿Say: "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth; indeed He is ever Forgiving, Merciful."﴾ ﴿And they said: "What is with this Messenger that he eats food as we eat and walks in the markets"﴾, seeking livelihood, [In the second copy there is an addition: "as we walk."] ﴿"Why has an angel not been sent down to him to accompany him as a warner?"﴾, confirming him; ﴿"or a treasure be thrown to him, that he may spend from it, so that he need not busy himself with seeking livelihood"﴾; ﴿"or he have a garden from which he eats"﴾. This is the reading of the majority. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with a nun, meaning "we eat."

﴿And the wrongdoers said: "You follow only a man affected by sorcery."﴾ This verse was revealed concerning the story of Ibn Abi Umayya, and its mention has already passed in Bani Isra'il.

﴿Look, O Muhammad, how they have struck for you the examples, so they have strayed, and they cannot find a way﴾ to guidance or an escape from misguidance. Allah informs that they hold fast to ignorance and error, turning away from right guidance and correctness, while they were nonetheless obligated to accept the truth. Thus it is established that the capacity by which they stray is other than the capacity by which guidance and faith are attained.

﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that﴾, that is, than what they said, according to Mujahid. Ikrimah related from Ibn Abbas, who said: It means better than walking in the markets and seeking livelihood. Then He explained what that better thing is, saying the Exalted: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾, that is, lofty houses; it is called a palace (qasr) because it confines (qasara) and prevents access to it. The reciters differed concerning His saying ﴿and He will give﴾: Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir and Asim, through the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, read it with a raised final letter, while the others read it with a jussive, on the position of the conditional clause in His saying ﴿if He wills, He will give﴾.

[We were informed] [Not in the manuscript.] Abu Amr Ahmad ibn Abi Ahmad ibn Hamdun al-Nisaburi informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Bukhari informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd ibn Farwa al-Bukhari told us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa Ishaq ibn Bishr al-Bukhari told us, saying: Juwaybir told us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the polytheists reproached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with poverty, saying: ﴿What is with this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets?﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) grieved over that, and Gabriel descended to him from his Lord, consoling him, and said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. The Lord of Might sends you peace and says to you: ﴿We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾," and they seek livelihood in the world.

He said: While Gabriel (peace be upon him) and the Prophet (ﷺ) were conversing, Gabriel melted until he became like a hirda. It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is a hirda?" He said: "A lizard." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Gabriel, what is wrong with you, that you have melted until you became like a hirda?" He said: "O Muhammad, a door of the doors of heaven has been opened which had never been opened before, and the angel has been moved. If it is opened, it is either mercy or punishment, and I fear that your people will be punished for their reproach of you with poverty." The Prophet (ﷺ) and Gabriel (peace be upon him) then began to weep, when Gabriel returned and said: "O Muhammad, rejoice! This is Ridwan, the keeper of Paradise, who has come to you with the good pleasure of your Lord." Ridwan came and greeted him, then said: "O Muhammad, the Lord of Might sends you peace"—and with him was a casket of light, shining—"and your Lord says to you: These are the keys to the treasuries of the world, together with what will not be diminished for you of what is with Me in the Hereafter, equal to the wing of a mosquito." The Prophet (ﷺ) looked at Gabriel (peace be upon him) as one seeking his counsel, and Gabriel struck the earth with his hand and said: "Be humble before Allah." He said: "O Ridwan, I have no need of it. Poverty is more beloved to me, and that I be a patient, grateful servant." Ridwan said: "You are right; may Allah make you right."

A call came from heaven, and Gabriel raised his head, and behold, the heavens had opened their doors up to the Throne. Allah the Exalted revealed to the Garden of Eden that it should lower a branch of its boughs over him, upon which was a cluster, upon which was a bough of green chrysolite, with seventy thousand red rubies. Gabriel said: "O Muhammad, raise your gaze." He raised it and saw the dwellings and chambers of the prophets, and behold, his dwelling was above the dwellings of the prophets, a special excellence for him, and a caller called: "Are you pleased, O Muhammad?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am pleased. So make what you intended to give me in this world a treasure with You for intercession on the Day of Resurrection." [Asbab Nuzul al-Ayat, al-Wahidi al-Naysaburi: 225.] [77]

They narrate that this verse was revealed by Ridwan: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾.

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 25, verses 11–20:**

﴿Nay, they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing fire for those who deny the Hour. When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring.﴾ *Taghayyuz* (fury, seething) means its boiling and surging, like an angry man whose chest boils with rage. *Zafir* is the roaring. The meaning of His saying ﴿they will hear its raging﴾ is that the sound of the fury comes from its blazing and intensity. Qutrub said: "Fury is not heard. The meaning is: they will see its fury and hear its roaring." A poet said:

*"And I saw your husband in battle,*
*girding a sword and a spear."*

That is, carrying a spear.

Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Kharja told us, saying: Abu Jaʿfar ibn Abi Shayba told us, saying: My paternal uncle Abu Bakr told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid told us, from al-Asbagh ibn Zayd al-Warraq, from Khalid ibn Kathir, from Khalid ibn Duraik, from a man among the companions of the Messenger of Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in Hell between its two eyes." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, does Hell have two eyes?" He said: "Yes. Have you not heard the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring﴾?" [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/7.] [78]

﴿And when they are thrown into a narrow place within it, bound together﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it narrows upon them as the butt of a spear (*al-zajj*) is confined within the spear.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim told us, saying: It was read to Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Nafiʿ informed me, from Yahya ibn Abi Usayd, who traced the report to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he was asked about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when they are thrown into a narrow place within it﴾, and he said: "By Him in Whose hand is my soul, they will be forced into the Fire as a peg is forced into a wall, bound together and shackled, their hands joined to their necks in chains." [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/323.] [79]

From this comes the word *qarn* for a rope, and it was said: they are bound with the devils in chains and shackles.

﴿There they will cry out for destruction﴾: *thubur* means ruin. This is from Ibn ʿAbbas; according to al-Dahhak it means perdition.

Hammad narrated from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first to be clothed in a garment of Fire is Iblis. He places it upon his brows and drags it behind him, and his offspring follow behind him, and he says: 'O my ruin!' and they call out: 'O our ruin!' until they line up (in some copies: *yaqifu*) at the Fire. Then it is said to them: ﴿Do not cry out for one destruction today, but cry out for many destructions.﴾ Say: ﴿Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the righteous have been promised? It shall be a reward and a final destination for them. Therein they shall have whatever they wish, abiding forever. It is a promise incumbent upon your Lord, to be asked for.﴾" And that is because the believers asked their Lord for this in the world when they said: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾ [Surah Al ʿImran: 194]. So Allah, the Exalted, said: the giving of the Garden of Eternity by Allah to the believers is a promise He made in return for their obedience to Him in the world and their asking Him for it. [Musnad Ahmad: 3/152.] [Note: the source of this passage is cited by al-Tha'labi as above.]

Some of the grammarians said: it means a binding promise (*waʿdan wajiban*), because what is asked for is obligatory even if it is not asked, like their saying. The parallel is the Arabs' saying: "I will certainly give you a thousand, a promise to be asked" (*waʿdan masʾulan*), meaning it is owed to you, so you ask for it.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu ʿAli ibn Hanash [in the second copy: Habish] the reciter told us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl the reciter told us, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Jaʿfar ibn Musafir told us, saying: Yahya ibn Hassan told us, saying: Rushd ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Harith told us, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿It is a promise incumbent upon your Lord, to be asked for.﴾ He said: The angels ask this for them by their saying: ﴿And admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them﴾ [Surah Ghafir: 8].

﴿And on the Day He gathers them, and what they worshipped besides Allah﴾: Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn Kathir, Yaʿqub, Ayyub, Abu ʿUbayd, Abu Hatim, and Hafs read *yahshuruhum* with the *ya*; the rest read it with the *nun* (*nahshuruhum*). According to Mujahid, what is meant by ﴿what they worshipped﴾ is the angels, humans, and jinn. ʿIkrima and al-Dahhak said: it means the idols. ﴿Then He will say﴾: Ibn ʿAmir reads it with the *nun* (*naqulu*); others read it with the *ya* (*yaqulu*). He says to those being worshipped besides Allah: ﴿Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?﴾ They will say: ﴿Glory be to You! It was not for us to take any protectors besides You﴾, meaning: it was not fitting for us to take as allies Your enemies. Rather: ﴿You are our Protector, apart from them.﴾ Al-Hasan and Abu Jaʿfar read *an nattakhidha* with a *damma* on the *nun* and a *fatha* on the *kha'* (*an nuttakhadha*).

Abu ʿUbayd said: This is not permissible, because Allah has mentioned *min* (مِنْ) twice; if it were as they say, it would have been: *an nattakhidha min dunika awliyaʾa* (without the second *min*). Others said: the second *min* is a *silah* (a grammatically superfluous particle).

﴿But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment, until they forgot the Reminder﴾, that is, in the world, with health and blessings. *Al-dhikr* (the Reminder) means they abandoned the Qur'an and did not act upon what is in it. It was also said: it means the Messenger; it was said: Islam; it was said: monotheism (*tawhid*); and it was said: the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted.

﴿And they were a people ruined (*bur*)﴾: that is, perishing, overcome by wretchedness and abandonment. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: *bur* is one who has no good in him at all. Abu ʿUbayd said: its root is from *al-bawar*, which is slump and corruption, and from it come *bawar al-ayyim* (the unmarried woman's state of being unwanted) and *bawar al-silʿa* (the goods being unsold). It is a verbal noun like *al-zur*, in which the singular, dual, plural, feminine, and masculine are the same. Ibn al-Zaʿbari said:

*"O Messenger of the King, my tongue*
*is mending what I tore; and I am ruined."*

[Taj al-ʿArus: 3/60.]

It was also said that it is the plural of *ba'ir* (ruined one). It is said: their dwellings became *bur*, meaning empty, with nothing in them.

Then Allah, the Exalted, will say to them when the objects of worship disown them: ﴿They have indeed denied you in what you say﴾, that they were gods. ﴿So you cannot avert﴾ — the common readers recite it with the *ya*, meaning the gods; Hafs recites it with the *ta'* (*tastatiʿuna*), meaning the worshippers — ﴿[the punishment] nor help﴾, meaning averting the punishment from them, nor helping themselves.

Yunus said: *al-sarf* means a stratagem, and from it the Arabs say: "He is adept (*li-yatasarraf*)," meaning he devises a stratagem. Al-Asmaʿi said: *al-sarf* is repentance, and *al-ʿadl* is ransom.

﴿And whoever among you wrongs﴾, that is, associates others with Allah, ﴿We shall make him taste a great punishment.﴾

﴿And We did not send before you, O Muhammad, any messengers except that they﴾ — the people of meaning (*ahl al-maʿani*) said: *illa* here is with the sense of "it was said that they..." — ﴿ate food and walked in the markets.﴾ The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾. It was also said: the meaning is "except that they..." This is a reply to the polytheists' saying: ﴿What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets?﴾

﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others﴾: the sick is a trial for the healthy, the afflicted is a trial for the well, and the poor is a trial for the rich. The sick man says: "If Allah willed, He would have made me healthy like so-and-so." The poor man says: "If Allah willed, He would have made me rich like so-and-so." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "I have made some of you a trial for others so that you may be patient over what you hear from them and see of their opposition, and follow guidance without My giving them worldly wealth for it. Had I willed to make the world accompany My messengers so that they would not oppose, I would have done so. But I decreed that I would test the servants through you and test you through them."

Abu al-Qasim ʿAbd al-Khaliq ibn ʿAli informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Yusuf in Bukhara informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Jumʿan informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa told us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Yahya told us, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Woe to the learned from the ignorant, woe to the ignorant from the learned; woe to the owner from the owned, woe to the owned from the owner; woe to the strong from the weak, woe to the weak from the strong; woe to the ruler from the subjects, woe to the subjects from the ruler — some of them a trial for others." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others﴾ [80].

﴿Will you be patient?﴾ And your Lord is ever Seeing. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/18.] Muqatil said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn ʿUqba, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. When they saw Abu Dharr, Ibn Mas'ud, ʿAmmar, Bilal, Suhayb, ʿAmir ibn Fuhayra, Mihjaʿ the freed slave of ʿUmar, Jabr the slave of Ibn al-Hadrami, and others below them, they said: "Shall we become Muslims and be like these?" So Allah, the Exalted, revealed, addressing these believers: ﴿Will you be patient?﴾, meaning in this state of hardship and poverty. ﴿And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾, of the one who is patient and the one who despairs, and of the one who believes and the one who does not believe.

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, does Hell have two eyes?" He said: "Yes. Have you not heard the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring﴾?" [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/7.] [78]

﴿And when they are thrown into a narrow place within it, bound together﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it narrows upon them as the butt of a spear (*al-zajj*) is confined within the spear.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim told us, saying: It was read to Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Nafiʿ informed me, from Yahya ibn Abi Usayd, who traced the report to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he was asked about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when they are thrown into a narrow place within it﴾, and he said: "By Him in Whose hand is my soul, they will be forced into the Fire as a peg is forced into a wall, bound together and shackled, their hands joined to their necks in chains." [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/323.] [79]

From this comes the word *qarn* for a rope, and it was said: they are bound with the devils in chains and shackles.

﴿There they will cry out for destruction﴾: *thubur* means ruin. This is from Ibn ʿAbbas; according to al-Dahhak it means perdition.

Hammad narrated from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first to be clothed in a garment of Fire is Iblis. He places it upon his brows and drags it behind him, and his offspring follow behind him, and he says: 'O my ruin!' and they call out: 'O our ruin!' until they line up (in some copies: *yaqifu*) at the Fire. Then it is said to them: ﴿Do not cry out for one destruction today, but cry out for many destructions.﴾ Say: ﴿Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which the righteous have been promised? It shall be a reward and a final destination for them. Therein they shall have whatever they wish, abiding forever. It is a promise incumbent upon your Lord, to be asked for.﴾" And that is because the believers asked their Lord for this in the world when they said: ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾ [Surah Al ʿImran: 194]. So Allah, the Exalted, said: the giving of the Garden of Eternity by Allah to the believers is a promise He made in return for their obedience to Him in the world and their asking Him for it. [Musnad Ahmad: 3/152.] [Note: the source of this passage is cited by al-Tha'labi as above.]

Some of the grammarians said: it means a binding promise (*waʿdan wajiban*), because what is asked for is obligatory even if it is not asked, like their saying. The parallel is the Arabs' saying: "I will certainly give you a thousand, a promise to be asked" (*waʿdan masʾulan*), meaning it is owed to you, so you ask for it.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu ʿAli ibn Hanash [in the second copy: Habish] the reciter told us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl the reciter told us, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Jaʿfar ibn Musafir told us, saying: Yahya ibn Hassan told us, saying: Rushd ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Harith told us, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿It is a promise incumbent upon your Lord, to be asked for.﴾ He said: The angels ask this for them by their saying: ﴿And admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them﴾ [Surah Ghafir: 8].

﴿And on the Day He gathers them, and what they worshipped besides Allah﴾: Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn Kathir, Yaʿqub, Ayyub, Abu ʿUbayd, Abu Hatim, and Hafs read *yahshuruhum* with the *ya*; the rest read it with the *nun* (*nahshuruhum*). According to Mujahid, what is meant by ﴿what they worshipped﴾ is the angels, humans, and jinn. ʿIkrima and al-Dahhak said: it means the idols. ﴿Then He will say﴾: Ibn ʿAmir reads it with the *nun* (*naqulu*); others read it with the *ya* (*yaqulu*). He says to those being worshipped besides Allah: ﴿Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?﴾ They will say: ﴿Glory be to You! It was not for us to take any protectors besides You﴾, meaning: it was not fitting for us to take as allies Your enemies. Rather: ﴿You are our Protector, apart from them.﴾ Al-Hasan and Abu Jaʿfar read *an nattakhidha* with a *damma* on the *nun* and a *fatha* on the *kha'* (*an nuttakhadha*).

Abu ʿUbayd said: This is not permissible, because Allah has mentioned *min* (مِنْ) twice; if it were as they say, it would have been: *an nattakhidha min dunika awliyaʾa* (without the second *min*). Others said: the second *min* is a *silah* (a grammatically superfluous particle).

﴿But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment, until they forgot the Reminder﴾, that is, in the world, with health and blessings. *Al-dhikr* (the Reminder) means they abandoned the Qur'an and did not act upon what is in it. It was also said: it means the Messenger; it was said: Islam; it was said: monotheism (*tawhid*); and it was said: the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted.

﴿And they were a people ruined (*bur*)﴾: that is, perishing, overcome by wretchedness and abandonment. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: *bur* is one who has no good in him at all. Abu ʿUbayd said: its root is from *al-bawar*, which is slump and corruption, and from it come *bawar al-ayyim* (the unmarried woman's state of being unwanted) and *bawar al-silʿa* (the goods being unsold). It is a verbal noun like *al-zur*, in which the singular, dual, plural, feminine, and masculine are the same. Ibn al-Zaʿbari said:

*"O Messenger of the King, my tongue*
*is mending what I tore; and I am ruined."*

[Taj al-ʿArus: 3/60.]

It was also said that it is the plural of *ba'ir* (ruined one). It is said: their dwellings became *bur*, meaning empty, with nothing in them.

Then Allah, the Exalted, will say to them when the objects of worship disown them: ﴿They have indeed denied you in what you say﴾, that they were gods. ﴿So you cannot avert﴾ — the common readers recite it with the *ya*, meaning the gods; Hafs recites it with the *ta'* (*tastatiʿuna*), meaning the worshippers — ﴿[the punishment] nor help﴾, meaning averting the punishment from them, nor helping themselves.

Yunus said: *al-sarf* means a stratagem, and from it the Arabs say: "He is adept (*li-yatasarraf*)," meaning he devises a stratagem. Al-Asmaʿi said: *al-sarf* is repentance, and *al-ʿadl* is ransom.

﴿And whoever among you wrongs﴾, that is, associates others with Allah, ﴿We shall make him taste a great punishment.﴾

﴿And We did not send before you, O Muhammad, any messengers except that they﴾ — the people of meaning (*ahl al-maʿani*) said: *illa* here is with the sense of "it was said that they..." — ﴿ate food and walked in the markets.﴾ The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾. It was also said: the meaning is "except that they..." This is a reply to the polytheists' saying: ﴿What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets?﴾

﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others﴾: the sick is a trial for the healthy, the afflicted is a trial for the well, and the poor is a trial for the rich. The sick man says: "If Allah willed, He would have made me healthy like so-and-so." The poor man says: "If Allah willed, He would have made me rich like so-and-so." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "I have made some of you a trial for others so that you may be patient over what you hear from them and see of their opposition, and follow guidance without My giving them worldly wealth for it. Had I willed to make the world accompany My messengers so that they would not oppose, I would have done so. But I decreed that I would test the servants through you and test you through them."

Abu al-Qasim ʿAbd al-Khaliq ibn ʿAli informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Yusuf in Bukhara informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Jumʿan informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa told us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Yahya told us, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from al-Hasan, from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Woe to the learned from the ignorant, woe to the ignorant from the learned; woe to the owner from the owned, woe to the owned from the owner; woe to the strong from the weak, woe to the weak from the strong; woe to the ruler from the subjects, woe to the subjects from the ruler — some of them a trial for others." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others﴾ [80].

﴿Will you be patient?﴾ And your Lord is ever Seeing. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/18.] Muqatil said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn ʿUqba, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. When they saw Abu Dharr, Ibn Mas'ud, ʿAmmar, Bilal, Suhayb, ʿAmir ibn Fuhayra, Mihjaʿ the freed slave of ʿUmar, Jabr the slave of Ibn al-Hadrami, and others below them, they said: "Shall we become Muslims and be like these?" So Allah, the Exalted, revealed, addressing these believers: ﴿Will you be patient?﴾, meaning in this state of hardship and poverty. ﴿And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾, of the one who is patient and the one who despairs, and of the one who believes and the one who does not believe.

**Al-Tha'labi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 25, verses 21–34:**

﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say: "Why were the angels not sent down to us, so that they could tell us that Muhammad is truthful and right? Or [why] do we not see our Lord, so that He could tell us of that?"﴾ Its parallel is His saying, ﴿And they say, "We will never believe you"﴾, up to His saying ﴿and the angels, as a company.﴾

God the Exalted said, ﴿They have been arrogant within themselves by this statement, and have committed great transgression.﴾ Muqatil said: they went to extremes in their speech. Al-'Utuw (transgression) means the gravest disbelief and the most shameful wrongdoing.

﴿On the day they see the angels﴾, at death and on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿there will be no good news that day for the criminals﴾, meaning the disbelievers. ﴿And they will say﴾, meaning the angels to the criminals, ﴿"A forbidden barrier, forbidden."﴾ That is, it is forbidden and prohibited for you to receive good tidings. It was also said: the Garden is forbidden to you. Some said: this is the speech of the disbelievers to the angels. Ibn Jurayj said: when the Arabs were struck by hardship or saw something they disliked, they would say, "Hijran mahjuran (a forbidden barrier, forbidden)." So they said this when they saw the angels. Mujahid said: it means "'awdhan mu'adhan (a refuge and a protection)", seeking refuge from the angels.

﴿And We turn to what they did of deeds, and We make it scattered dust.﴾ That is, void, without reward, because they did not do it for God the Exalted, but did it for Satan. The exegetes differed concerning al-haba' (scattered dust). Some said: it is what is seen in the openings of windows from the sunlight, like dust, which cannot be touched by hands and is not seen in shade. This is the view of al-Hasan, 'Ikrima and Mujahid.

Qatada and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is what the winds blow away and scatter of dust and debris of trees. This is the narration of 'Ata' al-Khurasani from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: it is dust. Al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas said: it is spilled water. Muqatil said: it is what rises from the hooves of animals. Al-manthur (scattered) means dispersed.

﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day are better in dwelling﴾ than these polytheists, the arrogant ones who boast of their wealth, ﴿and better in resting place﴾, a place of midday rest. This is by way of estimation. The exegetes said: it means that the people of the Garden will not pass through the Hereafter except for the measure of the appointed time of the day from its beginning until the time of midday rest, until they settle in their dwellings in the Garden.

Ibn Mas'ud said: the day of Resurrection will not reach midday until these people rest in the Garden and those people rest in the Fire. And he recited: ﴿Then indeed their return is to the Hellfire.﴾ That is how he used to recite it. Ibn 'Abbas said concerning this verse: the reckoning from that day is at its beginning. And "the people" said, when they said it, in their dwellings in the Garden.

Ibn Wahb narrated from 'Amr ibn al-Harith that Sa'id al-Sawwaf, or al-Sarraf, related to him that it had reached him that the Day of Resurrection will be shortened for the believers until it is like the period between the 'Asr prayer and sunset, and that they will rest in the gardens of the Garden until people are finished. And he recited this verse.

﴿And the Day when the heaven will be split open with clouds﴾. Abu 'Amr and the people of Kufa recited it with a light shin (tashdid absent), as an elision (hadhf), and the lightening is here and in Surah Qaf. The others recited it with the doubled shin in both places, meaning "the heaven will split open with the clouds," that is, "from the clouds." The bā' (with) and 'an (from) alternate, as one says "I shot from the bow" and "I shot with the bow," with the same meaning.

The exegetes said: it is a white, thin cloud, like a mist. It was not for the Children of Israel in their wandering. It is the one of which God the Exalted said: ﴿Do they only await that God should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels?﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 210].

﴿And the angels will be sent down, a sending down.﴾ This is the recitation of the general body of readers. Ibn Kathir recited "wa-nazzalu" with two nuns, and "al-malaika" in the accusative. ﴿Sovereignty on that day belongs to the Most Merciful﴾, pure, and the kingdoms of all others will have perished. ﴿And it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾, hard and severe. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿So that Day will be a difficult day, for the disbelievers, not easy﴾ [Surah al-Muddaththir: 9–10]. The address indicates that for the believers it will be easy.

In a hadith: indeed, on the Day of Resurrection it is made easy for the believer until it is lighter for him than an obligatory prayer he prayed in the house of the world.

﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾, the verse.

It was revealed concerning 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it and Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and the two were close friends. 'Uqba would not return from a journey without preparing food, and he would invite the nobles of his people. He used to frequently sit with the Prophet (ﷺ). One day he returned from his journey, prepared food, and invited the people, and he invited the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to his meal. When the food was brought, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I will not eat of your food until you bear witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God." 'Uqba said: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God." So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ate of his food. Ubayy ibn Khalaf was absent. When he was informed of the story, he said: "You have apostatized, O 'Uqba!" He said: "No, by God, I have not apostatized, but a man came to me and refused to eat of my food unless I bore witness for him. I was ashamed that he should leave my house without eating, so I bore witness for him, and he ate."

Ubayy said: "I will not be pleased with you ever, unless you go to him, spit in his face, and trample his neck." 'Uqba did that, and he took the afterbirth of an animal and threw it between his shoulders. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "If I meet you outside Makkah, I will certainly strike your head with the sword." So 'Uqba was killed in cold blood on the day of Badr. As for Ubayy ibn Khalaf, the Prophet (ﷺ) killed him with his own hand on the day of Uhud in the duel, and God revealed this verse concerning the two of them. [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/68.]

Al-Dahhak said: when 'Uqba spat in the face of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his spittle returned to his own face and split into two parts and burned his cheeks, and the mark of that remained on him until death.

'Ata' al-Khurasani narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf used to attend the Prophet (ﷺ) and sit with him and listen to his speech without believing in him. 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it rebuked him for that, and this verse was revealed.

Al-Sha'bi said: 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it was a close friend of Umayya ibn Khalaf. 'Uqba embraced Islam, so Umayya said: "My face is forbidden to your face if you pledge allegiance to Muhammad." So he disbelieved and apostatized, to please Umayya, and God the Exalted revealed: ﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾,

meaning the disbeliever 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it, [in one copy there is an addition: "ibn Umayya ibn 'Abd Shams ibn 'Abd Manaf"] biting on his hands in regret and remorse over what he neglected regarding God's right, and ruining himself through disobedience and disbelief in God, because of obedience to his close friend who turned him away from the path of his Lord. ﴿He will say: "Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger!"﴾, Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend!﴾ [Abu 'Amr read the "ta'" of "yaa laytani" with a fatha.] He means Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi. ﴿He led me astray from the Reminder﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the Messenger, ﴿after it had come to me.﴾ ﴿And Satan is ever, for man, a deserter﴾, meaning every rebellious, insolent one among the jinn, and everyone who turns away from the path of God and is obeyed in disobedience to Him is a devil. He will forsake him at the descent of the trial and punishment upon him.

The ruling of these verses is general for every two friends who gather in disobedience to God. Therefore some scholars said: Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far recited to me, saying: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn al-Siddiq recited to us, saying: Abu Wa'ila 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Husayn recited to us:

Avoid the companion of evil, and cut his ties,
If you cannot escape him, then keep your distance.
And love the beloved of truth, and beware his deceit,
You will obtain from him the purity of affection, so long as you do not dispute with him.
In gray hair there is what restrains the forbearing from youthful folly,
When its fires have kindled in his cheeks. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/26.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to me, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hamidi recited to me:

Keep company with the best of people wherever you meet them,
The best companion is the one who is chaste.
People are like dirhams that you have sorted,
So you find in them silver and counterfeit. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/26.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, the exegete, informed us, saying: Abu Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Haska narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: 'Asim narrated to us, from Abu Kabsha, who said:

I heard Abu Musa say from the pulpit: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of a good companion is like a perfume seller: if he does not give you some, you will still be enveloped by his fragrance. And the likeness of a bad companion is like a blacksmith: if he does not burn your clothes, you will still be enveloped by his smoke."

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib narrated to us, verbally, in the year 388 [AH], saying: Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hayyan ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Ali al-Khaladi informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Saqr al-Sukkari narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Muhammad al-Nabati narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Harith ibn Wajih say: I heard Malik ibn Dinar say: Indeed, carrying stones with the righteous is better for you than eating sweetmeats with the wicked.

﴿And the Messenger will say﴾, meaning, and the Messenger will say on that day: ﴿"My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as deserted (mahjur)."﴾ That is, they said false things about it, claiming that it is sorcery, poetry, and idle talk. Mahjur is from hujr (abusive speech), which is evil speech, according to al-Nakha'i and Mujahid.

Others said: it is from hijran (abandonment), that is, they turned away from it and left it, so they did not believe in it and did not act upon what it contains.

Abu al-Tayyib al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Hatimi and Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Khuza'i informed us, both saying: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Uqba al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim al-Khidr ibn Aban al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudba Ibrahim ibn Hudba narrated to us, saying: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever learns the Qur'an and teaches it, and hangs a copy of the mushaf without attending to it or looking into it, will come on the Day of Resurrection hanging by it, saying: 'O Lord of the worlds, this servant of Yours has taken me as deserted. Judge between me and him.'"

﴿Thus﴾, that is, just as We have made for you, O Muhammad, enemies, from among the polytheists of your people, ﴿so We have made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals﴾, that is, from among the polytheists of his people. So be patient with My command, as they were patient, for I am guiding you and supporting you against those who oppose you.

﴿And sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper﴾, as circumstantial accusatives (ḥāl and tamyīz). ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾, to Muhammad, ﴿just as the Torah was sent down to Moses, the Psalms to David, and the Gospel to Jesus, all at once.﴾ God the Exalted said: ﴿Thus [it is] so that We may strengthen your heart by it﴾, that We may fortify your heart with it, so that you may understand it and memorize it. For the books were sent down to prophets who could write and read, whereas the Qur'an was sent down to an unlettered prophet. Also, the Qur'an contains the abrogating and the abrogated, and some of it is an answer to those who asked about matters. So We divided it so that it would be easier for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to retain and easier for one who knows it.

﴿And We arranged it in gradual arrangement (tartil)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "wa-rattalnahu" means "wa-rassalnahu (We sent it down in portions)". Al-Nakha'i and al-Hasan said: "We divided it into divisions, verse after verse and portion after portion." Between its beginning and its end was about twenty-three years. Ibn Zayd said: "We explained it (fassarnahu) as an explanation." Tartil means clarification, in a flowing and deliberate manner.

﴿And they will not bring you﴾, O Muhammad, meaning these polytheists, ﴿any argument to undermine your cause, except that We bring you the truth﴾, that is, that by which you repel what they bring and nullify it, ﴿and [with] the best explanation﴾, clarification and detail. Then He described the state of the polytheists and clarified their condition on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿Those﴾, meaning those ones, ﴿who will be gathered on their faces﴾, driven and dragged along, ﴿to Hell; those are worse in position and more astray in way.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Khurja narrated to us, saying: al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from Aws ibn Aws, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three groups: one third upon mounts, one third upon their faces, and one third upon their feet, walking in a walk."

[Musnad Ibn Rahawayh: 1/180.] [82]

**Al-Tha'labi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 25, verses 21–34:**

﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say: "Why were the angels not sent down to us, so that they could tell us that Muhammad is truthful and right? Or [why] do we not see our Lord, so that He could tell us of that?"﴾ Its parallel is His saying, ﴿And they say, "We will never believe you"﴾, up to His saying ﴿and the angels, as a company.﴾

God the Exalted said, ﴿They have been arrogant within themselves by this statement, and have committed great transgression.﴾ Muqatil said: they went to extremes in their speech. Al-'Utuw (transgression) means the gravest disbelief and the most shameful wrongdoing.

It was also said: the Garden is forbidden to you. Some said: this is the speech of the disbelievers to the angels. Ibn Jurayj said: when the Arabs were struck by hardship or saw something they disliked, they would say, "Hijran mahjuran (a forbidden barrier, forbidden)." So they said this when they saw the angels. Mujahid said: it means "'awdhan mu'adhan (a refuge and a protection)", seeking refuge from the angels.

﴿And We turn to what they did of deeds, and We make it scattered dust.﴾ That is, void, without reward, because they did not do it for God the Exalted, but did it for Satan. The exegetes differed concerning al-haba' (scattered dust). Some said: it is what is seen in the openings of windows from the sunlight, like dust, which cannot be touched by hands and is not seen in shade. This is the view of al-Hasan, 'Ikrima and Mujahid.

Qatada and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is what the winds blow away and scatter of dust and debris of trees. This is the narration of 'Ata' al-Khurasani from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: it is dust. Or [why] do we not see our Lord, so that He could tell us of that?"﴾ Its parallel is His saying, ﴿And they say, "We will never believe you"﴾, up to His saying ﴿and the angels, as a company.﴾

God the Exalted said, ﴿They have been arrogant within themselves by this statement, and have committed great transgression.﴾ Muqatil said: they went to extremes in their speech. Al-'Utuw (transgression) means the gravest disbelief and the most shameful wrongdoing.

﴿On the day they see the angels﴾, at death and on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿there will be no good news that day for the criminals﴾, meaning the disbelievers. ﴿And they will say﴾, meaning the angels to the criminals, ﴿"A forbidden barrier, forbidden."﴾ That is, it is forbidden and prohibited for you to receive good tidings. It was also said: the Garden is forbidden to you. Some said: this is the speech of the disbelievers to the angels. Ibn Jurayj said: when the Arabs were struck by hardship or saw something they disliked, they would say, "Hijran mahjuran (a forbidden barrier, forbidden)." So they said this when they saw the angels. Mujahid said: it means "'awdhan mu'adhan (a refuge and a protection)", seeking refuge from the angels.

﴿And We turn to what they did of deeds, and We make it scattered dust.﴾ That is, void, without reward, because they did not do it for God the Exalted, but did it for Satan. The exegetes differed concerning al-haba' (scattered dust). Some said: it is what is seen in the openings of windows from the sunlight, like dust, which cannot be touched by hands and is not seen in shade. This is the view of al-Hasan, 'Ikrima and Mujahid.

Qatada and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is what the winds blow away and scatter of dust and debris of trees. This is the narration of 'Ata' al-Khurasani from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: it is dust. Al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas said: it is spilled water. Muqatil said: it is what rises from the hooves of animals. Al-manthur (scattered) means dispersed.

﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day are better in dwelling﴾ than these polytheists, the arrogant ones who boast of their wealth, ﴿and better in resting place﴾, a place of midday rest. This is by way of estimation. The exegetes said: it means that the people of the Garden will not pass through the Hereafter except for the measure of the appointed time of the day from its beginning until the time of midday rest, until they settle in their dwellings in the Garden.

Ibn Mas'ud said: the day of Resurrection will not reach midday until these people rest in the Garden and those people rest in the Fire. And he recited: ﴿Then indeed their return is to the Hellfire.﴾ That is how he used to recite it. Ibn 'Abbas said concerning this verse: the reckoning from that day is at its beginning. And "the people" said, when they said it, in their dwellings in the Garden.

Ibn Wahb narrated from 'Amr ibn al-Harith that Sa'id al-Sawwaf, or al-Sarraf, related to him that it had reached him that the Day of Resurrection will be shortened for the believers until it is like the period between the 'Asr prayer and sunset, and that they will rest in the gardens of the Garden until people are finished. And he recited this verse.

﴿And the Day when the heaven will be split open with clouds﴾. Abu 'Amr and the people of Kufa recited it with a light shin (tashdid absent), as an elision (hadhf), and the lightening is here and in Surah Qaf. The others recited it with the doubled shin in both places, meaning "the heaven will split open with the clouds," that is, "from the clouds." The bā' (with) and 'an (from) alternate, as one says "I shot from the bow" and "I shot with the bow," with the same meaning.

The exegetes said: it is a white, thin cloud, like a mist. It was not for the Children of Israel in their wandering. It is the one of which God the Exalted said: ﴿Do they only await that God should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels?﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 210].

﴿And the angels will be sent down, a sending down.﴾ This is the recitation of the general body of readers. Ibn Kathir recited "wa-nazzalu" with two nuns, and "al-malaika" in the accusative. ﴿Sovereignty on that day belongs to the Most Merciful﴾, pure, and the kingdoms of all others will have perished. ﴿And it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾, hard and severe. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿So that Day will be a difficult day, for the disbelievers, not easy﴾ [Surah al-Muddaththir: 9–10]. The address indicates that for the believers it will be easy.

In a hadith: indeed, on the Day of Resurrection it is made easy for the believer until it is lighter for him than an obligatory prayer he prayed in the house of the world.

﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾, the verse.

It was revealed concerning 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it and Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and the two were close friends. 'Uqba would not return from a journey without preparing food, and he would invite the nobles of his people. He used to frequently sit with the Prophet (ﷺ). One day he returned from his journey, prepared food, and invited the people, and he invited the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to his meal. When the food was brought, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I will not eat of your food until you bear witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God." 'Uqba said: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God." So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ate of his food. Ubayy ibn Khalaf was absent. When he was informed of the story, he said: "You have apostatized, O 'Uqba!" He said: "No, by God, I have not apostatized, but a man came to me and refused to eat of my food unless I bore witness for him. I was ashamed that he should leave my house without eating, so I bore witness for him, and he ate."

Ubayy said: "I will not be pleased with you ever, unless you go to him, spit in his face, and trample his neck." 'Uqba did that, and he took the afterbirth of an animal and threw it between his shoulders. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "If I meet you outside Makkah, I will certainly strike your head with the sword." So 'Uqba was killed in cold blood on the day of Badr. As for Ubayy ibn Khalaf, the Prophet (ﷺ) killed him with his own hand on the day of Uhud in the duel, and God revealed this verse concerning the two of them. [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/68.]

Al-Dahhak said: when 'Uqba spat in the face of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his spittle returned to his own face and split into two parts and burned his cheeks, and the mark of that remained on him until death.

'Ata' al-Khurasani narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf used to attend the Prophet (ﷺ) and sit with him and listen to his speech without believing in him. 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it rebuked him for that, and this verse was revealed.

Al-Sha'bi said: 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it was a close friend of Umayya ibn Khalaf. 'Uqba embraced Islam, so Umayya said: "My face is forbidden to your face if you pledge allegiance to Muhammad." So he disbelieved and apostatized, to please Umayya, and God the Exalted revealed: ﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾,

meaning the disbeliever 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it, [in one copy there is an addition: "ibn Umayya ibn 'Abd Shams ibn 'Abd Manaf"] biting on his hands in regret and remorse over what he neglected regarding God's right, and ruining himself through disobedience and disbelief in God, because of obedience to his close friend who turned him away from the path of his Lord. ﴿He will say: "Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger!"﴾, Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend!﴾ [Abu 'Amr read the "ta'" of "yaa laytani" with a fatha.] He means Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi. ﴿He led me astray from the Reminder﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the Messenger, ﴿after it had come to me.﴾ ﴿And Satan is ever, for man, a deserter﴾, meaning every rebellious, insolent one among the jinn, and everyone who turns away from the path of God and is obeyed in disobedience to Him is a devil. He will forsake him at the descent of the trial and punishment upon him.

The ruling of these verses is general for every two friends who gather in disobedience to God. Therefore some scholars said: Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far recited to me, saying: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn al-Siddiq recited to us, saying: Abu Wa'ila 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Husayn recited to us:

Avoid the companion of evil, and cut his ties,
If you cannot escape him, then keep your distance.
And love the beloved of truth, and beware his deceit,
You will obtain from him the purity of affection, so long as you do not dispute with him.
In gray hair there is what restrains the forbearing from youthful folly,
When its fires have kindled in his cheeks. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/26.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to me, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hamidi recited to me:

Keep company with the best of people wherever you meet them,
The best companion is the one who is chaste.
People are like dirhams that you have sorted,
So you find in them silver and counterfeit. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/26.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, the exegete, informed us, saying: Abu Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Haska narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: 'Asim narrated to us, from Abu Kabsha, who said:

I heard Abu Musa say from the pulpit: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of a good companion is like a perfume seller: if he does not give you some, you will still be enveloped by his fragrance. And the likeness of a bad companion is like a blacksmith: if he does not burn your clothes, you will still be enveloped by his smoke."

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib narrated to us, verbally, in the year 388 [AH], saying: Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hayyan ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Ali al-Khaladi informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Saqr al-Sukkari narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Muhammad al-Nabati narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Harith ibn Wajih say: I heard Malik ibn Dinar say: Indeed, carrying stones with the righteous is better for you than eating sweetmeats with the wicked.

﴿And the Messenger will say﴾, meaning, and the Messenger will say on that day: ﴿"My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as deserted (mahjur)."﴾ That is, they said false things about it, claiming that it is sorcery, poetry, and idle talk. Mahjur is from hujr (abusive speech), which is evil speech, according to al-Nakha'i and Mujahid.

Others said: it is from hijran (abandonment), that is, they turned away from it and left it, so they did not believe in it and did not act upon what it contains.

Abu al-Tayyib al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Hatimi and Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Khuza'i informed us, both saying: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Uqba al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim al-Khidr ibn Aban al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudba Ibrahim ibn Hudba narrated to us, saying: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever learns the Qur'an and teaches it, and hangs a copy of the mushaf without attending to it or looking into it, will come on the Day of Resurrection hanging by it, saying: 'O Lord of the worlds, this servant of Yours has taken me as deserted. Judge between me and him.'"

﴿Thus﴾, that is, just as We have made for you, O Muhammad, enemies, from among the polytheists of your people, ﴿so We have made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals﴾, that is, from among the polytheists of his people. So be patient with My command, as they were patient, for I am guiding you and supporting you against those who oppose you.

﴿And sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper﴾, as circumstantial accusatives (ḥāl and tamyīz). ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾, to Muhammad, ﴿just as the Torah was sent down to Moses, the Psalms to David, and the Gospel to Jesus, all at once.﴾ God the Exalted said: ﴿Thus [it is] so that We may strengthen your heart by it﴾, that We may fortify your heart with it, so that you may understand it and memorize it. For the books were sent down to prophets who could write and read, whereas the Qur'an was sent down to an unlettered prophet. Also, the Qur'an contains the abrogating and the abrogated, and some of it is an answer to those who asked about matters. So We divided it so that it would be easier for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to retain and easier for one who knows it.

﴿And We arranged it in gradual arrangement (tartil)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "wa-rattalnahu" means "wa-rassalnahu (We sent it down in portions)". Al-Nakha'i and al-Hasan said: "We divided it into divisions, verse after verse and portion after portion." Between its beginning and its end was about twenty-three years. Ibn Zayd said: "We explained it (fassarnahu) as an explanation." Tartil means clarification, in a flowing and deliberate manner.

﴿And they will not bring you﴾, O Muhammad, meaning these polytheists, ﴿any argument to undermine your cause, except that We bring you the truth﴾, that is, that by which you repel what they bring and nullify it, ﴿and [with] the best explanation﴾, clarification and detail. Then He described the state of the polytheists and clarified their condition on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿Those﴾, meaning those ones, ﴿who will be gathered on their faces﴾, driven and dragged along, ﴿to Hell; those are worse in position and more astray in way.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Khurja narrated to us, saying: al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from Aws ibn Aws, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three groups: one third upon mounts, one third upon their faces, and one third upon their feet, walking in a walk."

[Musnad Ibn Rahawayh: 1/180.] [82]

I was ashamed that he should leave my house without eating, so I bore witness for him, and he ate."

Ubayy said: "I will not be pleased with you ever, unless you go to him, spit in his face, and trample his neck." Al-Sha'bi said: 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it was a close friend of Umayya ibn Khalaf. 'Uqba embraced Islam, so Umayya said: "My face is forbidden to your face if you pledge allegiance to Muhammad." So he disbelieved and apostatized, to please Umayya, and God the Exalted revealed: ﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾,

meaning the disbeliever 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it, [in one copy there is an addition: "ibn Umayya ibn 'Abd Shams ibn 'Abd Manaf"] biting on his hands in regret and remorse over what he neglected regarding God's right, and ruining himself through disobedience and disbelief in God, because of obedience to his close friend who turned him away from the path of his Lord. ﴿He will say: "Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger!"﴾, Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend!﴾ [Abu 'Amr read the "ta'" of "yaa laytani" with a fatha.] He means Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi. ﴿He led me astray from the Reminder﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the Messenger, ﴿after it had come to me.﴾ ﴿And Satan is ever, for man, a deserter﴾, meaning every rebellious, insolent one among the jinn, and everyone who turns away from the path of God and is obeyed in disobedience to Him is a devil. Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Khurja narrated to us, saying: al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from Aws ibn Aws, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three groups: one third upon mounts, one third upon their faces, and one third upon their feet, walking in a walk."

[Musnad Ibn Rahawayh: 1/180.] [82]

**Al-Tha'labi's commentary (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 25, verses 21–34:**

﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say: "Why were the angels not sent down to us, so that they could tell us that Muhammad is truthful and right? Or [why] do we not see our Lord, so that He could tell us of that?"﴾ Its parallel is His saying, ﴿And they say, "We will never believe you"﴾, up to His saying ﴿and the angels, as a company.﴾

God the Exalted said, ﴿They have been arrogant within themselves by this statement, and have committed great transgression.﴾ Muqatil said: they went to extremes in their speech. Al-'Utuw (transgression) means the gravest disbelief and the most shameful wrongdoing.

﴿On the day they see the angels﴾, at death and on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿there will be no good news that day for the criminals﴾, meaning the disbelievers. ﴿And they will say﴾, meaning the angels to the criminals, ﴿"A forbidden barrier, forbidden."﴾ That is, it is forbidden and prohibited for you to receive good tidings. It was also said: the Garden is forbidden to you. Some said: this is the speech of the disbelievers to the angels. Ibn Jurayj said: when the Arabs were struck by hardship or saw something they disliked, they would say, "Hijran mahjuran (a forbidden barrier, forbidden)." So they said this when they saw the angels. Mujahid said: it means "'awdhan mu'adhan (a refuge and a protection)", seeking refuge from the angels.

﴿And We turn to what they did of deeds, and We make it scattered dust.﴾ That is, void, without reward, because they did not do it for God the Exalted, but did it for Satan. The exegetes differed concerning al-haba' (scattered dust). Some said: it is what is seen in the openings of windows from the sunlight, like dust, which cannot be touched by hands and is not seen in shade. This is the view of al-Hasan, 'Ikrima and Mujahid.

Qatada and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is what the winds blow away and scatter of dust and debris of trees. This is the narration of 'Ata' al-Khurasani from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: it is dust. Al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas said: it is spilled water. Muqatil said: it is what rises from the hooves of animals. Al-manthur (scattered) means dispersed.

﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day are better in dwelling﴾ than these polytheists, the arrogant ones who boast of their wealth, ﴿and better in resting place﴾, a place of midday rest. This is by way of estimation. The exegetes said: it means that the people of the Garden will not pass through the Hereafter except for the measure of the appointed time of the day from its beginning until the time of midday rest, until they settle in their dwellings in the Garden.

Ibn Mas'ud said: the day of Resurrection will not reach midday until these people rest in the Garden and those people rest in the Fire. And he recited: ﴿Then indeed their return is to the Hellfire.﴾ That is how he used to recite it. Ibn 'Abbas said concerning this verse: the reckoning from that day is at its beginning. And "the people" said, when they said it, in their dwellings in the Garden.

Ibn Wahb narrated from 'Amr ibn al-Harith that Sa'id al-Sawwaf, or al-Sarraf, related to him that it had reached him that the Day of Resurrection will be shortened for the believers until it is like the period between the 'Asr prayer and sunset, and that they will rest in the gardens of the Garden until people are finished. And he recited this verse.

The others recited it with the doubled shin in both places, meaning "the heaven will split open with the clouds," that is, "from the clouds." The bā' (with) and 'an (from) alternate, as one says "I shot from the bow" and "I shot with the bow," with the same meaning.

The exegetes said: it is a white, thin cloud, like a mist. It was not for the Children of Israel in their wandering. It is the one of which God the Exalted said: ﴿Do they only await that God should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels?﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 210].

Ibn Kathir recited "wa-nazzalu" with two nuns, and "al-malaika" in the accusative. ﴿Sovereignty on that day belongs to the Most Merciful﴾, pure, and the kingdoms of all others will have perished. ﴿And it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾, hard and severe. And We certainly gave Musa the Book and appointed with him his brother Harun as a minister (wazir), meaning a helper and supporter. Then We said: "Go to the people who denied Our signs", meaning the Copts. In the verse there is an omitted element which is understood from the context, its estimated form being: so they denied both of them.
Then We destroyed them with complete destruction, meaning We annihilated them with total annihilation. And the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind, an admonition. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers in the Hereafter a painful punishment, in addition to the punishment that had already befallen them in this world.

As for ʿĀd and Thamud and the People of the Rass (al-Rass, the well), they have been disputed. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they were people of wells. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: they were the people of a well, sitting beside it, and they were herdsmen; they worshipped idols. God sent to them Shuʿayb, calling them to Islam. He came to them and invited them, but they persisted in their rebellion and in harming Shuʿayb, so God warned them of His punishment. While they were around the well in their dwellings, the well collapsed, swallowing them together with their homes and their possessions, and they all perished.

Qatadah said: al-Rass is a village in Falj al-Yamamah. They killed their prophet, so God destroyed them. Some of them said: they were the remnant of the people of Hud and the people of Salih, and they are the people of the well which God mentions in His saying: ﴿And a deserted well and a lofty palace﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 45].

Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn al-Kalbi and al-Khalil said: they had a prophet called Hanzalah ibn Safwan. In their land there was a mountain called Fatah, whose summit rose a mile into the sky. The ʿanqa' (a mythical bird) used to frequent it; it was the largest of birds and had every colour. They named it ʿanqa' because of the length of its neck. It would dwell on that mountain and swoop down on birds to eat them. One day it grew hungry, and birds were scarce, so it swooped on a child and carried him off. For this reason it was named ʿanqa' Maghrib, because it disappears (yaghrib) with what it takes and carries it away. Then it swooped on a girl once she had grown up, seized her and pressed her to its two small wings, apart from its two large wings, and flew away with her. They complained to their prophet, and he said: "O God, seize it and cut off its offspring." A thunderbolt struck it and it burned, leaving no trace. The Arabs mentioned it in their poetry. Then they killed their prophet, and God destroyed them.

Ka'b, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: they are the people of Ya-Sin, and al-Rass is a well at Antioch in which they killed Habib the carpenter; they were attributed to it, and they are the Rass. God mentioned them in Surah Ya-Sin. It was also said: they are the people of the trench (al-Ukhdud), and al-Rass is the trench they dug. ʿIkrimah said: they are a people who buried their prophet alive in a well. The evidence for this is what:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The first of mankind to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection will be a black slave. That is because God sent a prophet to the people of a town, and none of its people believed in him except that black slave. Then the people of the town attacked that prophet, dug a well for him, threw him into it, and then closed it over him with a huge stone. That black slave used to go out to gather firewood, carrying it on his back, then bring his firewood and sell it, buying with it food and drink. Then he would come to that well, lift that stone, God helping him to do so, and lower to him his food and drink, then replace the stone as it was."

He said: This went on for as long as God willed. Then one day he went out to gather firewood as he usually did, gathered his wood, bound his bundle and finished it. When he wished to lift it, he felt drowsy, lay down and slept, and God struck his ear for seven years. Then he woke, stretched, turned onto his other side and lay down, and God struck his ear for another seven years. Then he woke, lifted his bundle, and supposed he had slept only an hour of the day. He came to the town, sold his bundle, bought food and drink as he used to, then went to the pit in its place, looking for it, but did not find it, for matters had changed among his people there. They took him out and believed in him and confirmed him.

He said: The Prophet used to ask them about that black slave, "What became of him?" They would say to him, "We do not know," until God took that prophet. Then God woke the black slave from his sleep, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "That black slave is truly the first to enter Paradise."

[Fath al-Qadir – al-Shawkani: 4/78.] [83]

I say: This hadith mentions that they believed in their prophet and brought him out of his pit, so they should not be the ones meant by His saying ﴿and the people of the Rass﴾, because God, exalted is He, informed about the people of the Rass that He destroyed them with destruction, unless they were destroyed for innovations they introduced after their prophet whom they brought out of the pit and believed in; in that case this would be a valid view.

It has been reported from Commander of the Faithful [Bihar al-Anwar: 14/149] ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, concerning the story of the people of the Rass, what confirms the statement of ʿIkrimah and his interpretation, and it is what:

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-ʿAbidin narrated from his father, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, that a man of the nobles of Banu Tamim, called ʿAmr, came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, inform me about the people of the Rass: in what era were they? Where were their dwellings? Who was their king? Did God send a messenger to them? And by what were they destroyed? For I find their mention in the Book of God, but I do not find their account." ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, said to him: "You have asked about a matter that no one before you has asked me about, and no one after me will tell you of it."

The account of them, O brother of Tamim, is that they were a people who worshipped a pine tree called Shah Darakht, which Yafith ibn Nuh had planted at the edge of a spring called Dushab, which had sprouted for Nuh, peace be upon him, after the Flood. They were called the people of the Rass because they buried their prophet in the earth, and that was before Sulayman ibn Dawud. They had twelve villages on the bank of a river called al-Rass in the lands of the East, and the river was named after them. In that time there was no more abundant or sweeter river on earth, nor villages with more inhabitants or more prosperous. Their greatest city was Isfandmah, where their king resided; he was called Nirkuz ibn ʿAnur ibn Nawash ibn Sarun ibn Nimrod ibn Kanʿan. In it were the spring and the pine tree. They had planted, in every village, a seed from the cone of that pine, and the seed sprouted and became a great tree. They forbade drinking from the spring and the rivers, so neither they nor their livestock drank from them, and whoever did so they killed. They said: "It is the life of our gods, so no one should pluck from its seeds." They and their livestock drank from the river al-Rass on which their villages stood. In every month of the year, in every village, they held a festival to which its people gathered, and they stretched over the tree a veil of silk bearing all kinds of images. Then they brought sheep and cattle and slaughtered them as offerings to the tree, and they set fire to them with wood. When the smoke of those sacrifices rose into the air and blocked their view of the sky, they fell prostrate before the tree, weeping and imploring it to be pleased with them.

Satan would come, shake its branches and cry out from its trunk like a child: "I am pleased with you, my servants, so be content and let your eyes be cool." Then they would raise their heads, drink wine and play instruments, remaining so for their day and night. Then they would disperse. When the festival of their greatest town came, its young and old gathered; they set up a pavilion beside the pine and the spring and offered to it sacrifices many times more than they had offered to the tree in their villages. Then Iblis would come, shake the pine violently, and speak from within it with a booming voice, promising them and offering them more than all the devils had promised. They would raise their heads from prostration, filled with such joy and vigour that they could not recover from drinking and music, and they would remain so for twelve days and nights, corresponding to the number of their festivals in the year, and then disperse.

When their disbelief in God and their worship of other than Him grew long, God sent to them a prophet from the Children of Israel, of the offspring of Judah son of Jacob. He stayed among them a long time, calling them to the worship of God, exalted is He, and to recognition of His lordship, but they did not follow him.
