When he saw their extreme persistence in error and misguidance, and their refusal to accept what he called them to of guidance and righteousness, and he came to their greatest town, he said: "O Lord, Your servants have refused anything but to deny me and to disbelieve in You, and they have taken to worshipping a tree that neither benefits nor harms. So wither their tree entirely, and show them Your power and authority." In the morning the people found their whole tree withered. This alarmed them and they were divided into two groups: one group said, "The sorcery of your gods has done this—this man who claims to be the messenger of the Lord of heaven and earth to you, in order to turn your faces from your gods toward his god."

Another group said, "No, rather your gods became angry when they saw this man disparaging them, reviling them, and calling you to worship other than them, so they withdrew their beauty and radiance so that you would become angry for them, and they would take vengeance on him." Their opinion was unanimously to kill him. They made long tubes of lead with wide mouths and sent them down into the bottom of the spring, one above another, like conduits. They drained the water within, then dug at its bottom a narrow, deep well, sent their prophet down into it, and stopped its mouth with a huge rock. Then they removed the tubes from the water and said: "We hope now that our gods will be pleased with us, since they have seen that we have killed the one who reviled them and turned people from their worship, and buried him beneath their greatest one, so that they may be healed of him and their light and splendour return as they were." They remained most of that day hearing the groaning of their prophet, peace be upon him, as he said: "My master, You see the narrowness of my place and the severity of my distress. Have mercy on my weakness and my lack of strength, hasten the taking of my soul, and do not delay the answer to my prayer," until he died, peace be upon him.

God, exalted is He, said to Jibril: "These servants of Mine have been deceived by My forbearance, felt secure from My plotting, worshipped other than Me, and killed My messenger. I am the avenger of those who disobey Me and do not fear My punishment, and I have sworn that I will make them an example and a warning to the worlds." They were not alarmed, while they were at their festival, except by a violent, fierce, deep-red wind, which stripped them bare and left them bewildered. They pressed together, and then the earth beneath them became a stone of sulphur blazing, and a black cloud overshadowed them and rained down upon them like a red, flaming dome, and their bodies melted as lead melts in fire. We seek refuge with God from His anger and the reach of His vengeance.

Some scholars of the accounts of past peoples and the biographies of earlier generations said: "I have been told that there were two Rass. As for one of them, its people were nomads, dwellers of tents, and herdsmen. God sent to them a messenger, and they killed him. Then He sent them another messenger and supported him with a saint (wali), and they killed the messenger, and the saint struggled against them until he silenced them. They used to say, 'Our god is in the sea,' and they were on its shore. Every month a devil would come out to them from the sea, and they would slaughter before it and make it a festival. The saint said to them, 'Do you see: if your god, whom you worship, came out, and I called upon him and he answered me and I commanded him and he obeyed me, would you respond to what I call you to?' They said, 'Yes.' So they gave him their covenants and pledges upon that. They waited until that devil came out in the form of a fish, riding four fish, with a long neck raised up and something like a crown on its head. When they looked at it, they fell down prostrate. The saint went out to it and said, 'Come to me willingly or unwillingly, in the name of God the Generous.' Then it descended from its fish and the saint said to it, 'Come to me upon them, so that there may be no doubt among the people about its matter.' It came, and they brought it, dragging it and being dragged by it, until they reached the shore. Then they denied him after that, so God sent a wind upon them which flung them into the sea, and it flung into the sea their livestock and what they possessed of gold, silver and vessels. The righteous saint went to the sea and took the gold, silver and vessels and divided them equally among his companions, and the line of these people was cut off."

"As for the other Rass: they were a people who had a river called al-Rass, after which they were named. There were many prophets among them; scarcely did a prophet arise among them without being killed. That river was at the far edge of Adharbayjan, between it and Armenia: if you crossed it going back you entered the bounds of Armenia, and if you crossed it coming forward you entered the bounds of Adharbayjan. Those around them from Armenia worshipped idols, and those in front of them from Adharbayjan worshipped fire. They worshipped virgin maidens, and when one of them reached thirty years, they killed her and substituted another.

The breadth of their river was three farsakhs, and it rose each day and night until it reached the middle of the mountains around it. It did not settle on land or sea: when it left their boundary it would stop, turn, and return to them. God sent to them thirty prophets in one month, and they killed them all. Then God sent to them a prophet, supported him with His help, and sent with him a saint; he struggled against them for God with the struggle due to Him, and they rejected him openly. God sent Mikail, and this was at the time the seed falls into the field, when they were most in need of water. He caused their river to burst into the sea, so that what was at its bottom drained away, and he came to its springs from above and blocked them up.

God sent His helpers from the angels, five hundred thousand, and they dispersed what remained in the middle of the river. Then God commanded Jibril, who descended and left in their land no spring, no water, no river, without drying it up by God's permission. He commanded the Angel of Death, who went to the livestock and caused them to die in a single instant. He commanded the four winds, the south, the north, the east and the west, and they shattered whatever goods they had. God cast sleep upon them; then the four winds swept away all those goods, scattering them over the mountain peaks and the valley bottoms. As for their ornaments, silver or gold, or vessels, God commanded the earth and it swallowed them. They woke with no livestock, no property to return to, and no water to drink, and their crops were withered. Then a few of them believed in God, and God guided them to a cave in a mountain that had a path leading behind it; they were saved. They numbered twenty-one men, four women and two children. The rest of the men, women and children numbered six hundred thousand, and they died of thirst and hunger, and none of them remained.

Then the believing people returned to their dwellings and found that their upper parts had become their lower parts. They called upon God then, sincerely, that He would bring them crops, livestock and water, and make it little so that they would not transgress. God answered them in this, knowing their sincerity, and released their river for them and gave them more than they had asked.

Those people remained in obedience to God, outwardly and inwardly, until they passed away. Then after them came a generation who obeyed God outwardly but were hypocrites inwardly, and God gave them respite. Then their disobedience multiplied, so God set their enemy over them, who swiftly slew them, and a remnant was left. God then sent the plague upon them, and not one of them remained. Their river and dwellings remained for two hundred years with no one living in them.

Then God brought after that a new generation, who settled there and were righteous for some years. Then they introduced a foul practice: a man would call his daughter, his sister and his wife, and his neighbour and friend and brother would have intercourse with her, seeking by that piety and kinship. Then they advanced from that to another kind, where a man was content with a man and they abandoned women until they became lustful. A female demon came to them in the form of a woman; she was Dalhath, daughter of Iblis, sister of Satan—they were in one egg—and she made the riding of women upon one another appear attractive to them and taught them how to do it. Thus the origin of women mounting one another is from Dalhath. God then sent upon that generation a thunderbolt at the beginning of the night, a sinking of the earth at the end of the night, and a cry at sunrise, and not one of them remained, and their dwellings were destroyed."

Part of this story is corroborated by what:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: al-Hasan ibn Ismaʿil al-Dinawari told us... — Ibn Fanjawayh said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik told us; al-Hasan ibn Ismaʿil al-Dinawari told us; Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Malik al-Susi told us; Nasr ibn Hammad told us; ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, from Makhul, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Among the signs of the Hour is that men will suffice themselves with men and women with women, and that is sahq."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Abu al-Tayyib ibn Hafsawayh told us; ʿAbd Allah ibn Jami' told us; ʿUthman ibn Kharzadh told us; Salman ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman told us; al-Hakam ibn Yaʿla ibn ʿAta' told us; Muʿawiyah ibn ʿAmmar al-Dahni told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, concerning His saying ﴿and the people of the Rass﴾, who said: "The sahqat" (women who practise sahq).

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/33.] [84]

Al-Rass in the language of the Arabs means every excavated thing, such as a well, a mine, a grave and the like, and its plural is risas. The poet said:

"I have outstripped to the front with people of Tanabilah... digging the risas."

[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 19/20.]

Abu Ubayd said: al-Rass is every well that has not been lined with stones, bricks or wood.

﴿And We destroyed many generations between them.﴾ And to each We set forth parables, establishing the proof; yet We destroyed them only after warning and admonition. ﴿And each We utterly destroyed with complete destruction.﴾ That is, We annihilated them with annihilation. The historian said: al-Akhfash said: We shattered them into pieces.

﴿And indeed they have passed by the town upon which a rain of evil was rained down.﴾ That is, the rain of stones. It was the town of the people of Lot, and there were five towns. Allah, glorified is He, destroyed four of them and the fifth remained. Its name was Sughar, and its people did not do that vile deed.

﴿Had they not been seeing it?﴾ when they passed by it on their journeys, so that they would take heed and be mindful. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Rather, they did not expect to be raised.﴾ That is, they did not fear resurrection.

﴿And when they see you, they take you only for mockery.﴾ It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl: whenever he passed by his companions while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was present, he would say mockingly: ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger? He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in them.﴾ He almost turned us away from their worship. ﴿And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in the way.﴾ This is a warning to them.

﴿Have you seen one who has taken his desire as his god?﴾ This is because a man among the polytheists would worship a stone or an idol; if he saw something better than it, he would throw it away and take the other and worship it. Ibn Abbas said: "Hawa (desire) is a god worshipped besides Allah."

﴿Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾ a protector, preventing him from going out into this corruption. It was abrogated by the verse of jihad.

﴿Or do you think that most of them hear?﴾ what he says, the hearing of one seeking understanding, ﴿or reason?﴾ what they witness of proofs and signs. ﴿They are only like livestock; rather, they are further astray in the way.﴾ Because animals find their way to their pastures and watering places, and submit to their owners who feed and care for them, whereas these disbelievers do not recognize the path of truth and do not obey their Lord who created and provided for them.

﴿Have you not seen your Lord, how He extends the shade?﴾ Its meaning: have you not seen the extension of your Lord's shade? It is what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun. He made it extended because there is no sun with it, as He said of the shade of Paradise: ﴿and extended shade﴾, since there was no sun in it. ﴿And had He willed, He would have made it still, constant and fixed, not moving and not removed by the sun.﴾

Abu Ubayd said: the shade (zill) is what the sun has cancelled, and it is in the morning; and the fay' is what the sun has cancelled after its decline (zawal), and it was named fay' because it moves from the side of the east to the side of the west.

﴿Then We made the sun over it,﴾ that is, over the shade, ﴿an indicator.﴾ The meaning of its indicating it is that if there were no sun, the shade would not be known, since things are known by their opposites. The shade follows the sun in its lengthening and shortening, as the traveller follows the guide. When the sun rises, the shade shortens, and when it sinks, the shade lengthens. ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal.﴾ That is, the shade, by the sun that comes and cancels it. The meaning of His words "gradual" is light and swift. The word "qabd" means gathering scattered parts, and here it means a gentle transfer.

﴿And it is He who made the night for you as a garment,﴾ that is, a covering in which you conceal yourselves and rest. ﴿And sleep as rest,﴾ a repose for your bodies and a cessation of your labour. The root of sabt is cutting off, from which comes the day of Saturday (sabt) and sabtiyya sandals. ﴿And made the day a resurrection,﴾ that is, an awakening and life, in which you rise up and scatter for your affairs.

﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water,﴾ that is, pure in itself and purifying for others, ﴿that We may give life thereby to a dead land,﴾ "dead" is used rather than "dead (feminine)" because it refers to the place and the locality. Ka'b said: "Rain is the spirit of the earth." ﴿And that We may give it to drink﴾ — the common readers recite it with a dammed nun, while al-Mufaddal and al-Barjami narrated from Asim with a fatha on the nun, which is the reading of the Commander of the Faithful Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) — ﴿of what We have created, cattle and many people.﴾ Al-anasi is the plural of al-insan (human being); its original form was anasin, like bustan and basatin, and the ba' was substituted for the nun. It is also said to be a valid form, just as qarqur becomes qarariq and qarāqir.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Fanjawi informed me, saying: Makhlad ibn Ja'far al-Baqirhi narrated to us; al-Hasan ibn Alawi narrated to us; Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Juraij and Muqatil all said, and they traced it back to Ibn Mas'ud: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No year is more abundant in rain than another; rather, Allah distributes these provisions and places them in the lowest heaven in this rain, which descends each year in a known measure and known weight. But when a people commit sins, Allah diverts it to others; and when they all disobey, Allah diverts it to the deserts and the seas." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/57, with variation.] [85]

﴿And We have indeed distributed it among them,﴾ that is, the rain, ﴿year after year, and in one town rather than another.﴾ It is also said: We distributed it among them as heavy rain, drizzle, showers and fine mist. It is also said: the distribution refers to the wind.

﴿So that they may take heed, yet most people refused except disbelief,﴾ that is, denial. It is also said: it is their saying "such-and-such rain." ﴿And had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town,﴾ a messenger, and We would have distributed the warner among them just as We distributed the rain. In that case the burden of prophethood would be lighter on you, but We have laid upon you the weight of warning all the towns, so that by your patience in it you may merit what We have prepared for you of honour, dignity and high rank.

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers﴾ in what they call you to of worshipping their gods, approaching them, or flattering them, ﴿and strive against them with it﴾ — that is, with the Qur'an — ﴿a great striving.﴾

And We certainly gave Musa the Book and appointed with him his brother Harun as a minister (wazir), meaning a helper and supporter. Then We said: "Go to the people who denied Our signs", meaning the Copts. In the verse there is an omitted element which is understood from the context, its estimated form being: so they denied both of them.
Then We destroyed them with complete destruction, meaning We annihilated them with total annihilation. And the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind, an admonition. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers in the Hereafter a painful punishment, in addition to the punishment that had already befallen them in this world.

As for ʿĀd and Thamud and the People of the Rass (al-Rass, the well), they have been disputed. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they were people of wells. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: they were the people of a well, sitting beside it, and they were herdsmen; they worshipped idols. God sent to them Shuʿayb, calling them to Islam. He came to them and invited them, but they persisted in their rebellion and in harming Shuʿayb, so God warned them of His punishment. While they were around the well in their dwellings, the well collapsed, swallowing them together with their homes and their possessions, and they all perished.

Qatadah said: al-Rass is a village in Falj al-Yamamah. They killed their prophet, so God destroyed them. Some of them said: they were the remnant of the people of Hud and the people of Salih, and they are the people of the well which God mentions in His saying: ﴿And a deserted well and a lofty palace﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 45].

Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn al-Kalbi and al-Khalil said: they had a prophet called Hanzalah ibn Safwan. In their land there was a mountain called Fatah, whose summit rose a mile into the sky. The ʿanqa' (a mythical bird) used to frequent it; it was the largest of birds and had every colour. They named it ʿanqa' because of the length of its neck. It would dwell on that mountain and swoop down on birds to eat them. One day it grew hungry, and birds were scarce, so it swooped on a child and carried him off. For this reason it was named ʿanqa' Maghrib, because it disappears (yaghrib) with what it takes and carries it away. Then it swooped on a girl once she had grown up, seized her and pressed her to its two small wings, apart from its two large wings, and flew away with her. They complained to their prophet, and he said: "O God, seize it and cut off its offspring." A thunderbolt struck it and it burned, leaving no trace. The Arabs mentioned it in their poetry. Then they killed their prophet, and God destroyed them.

Ka'b, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: they are the people of Ya-Sin, and al-Rass is a well at Antioch in which they killed Habib the carpenter; they were attributed to it, and they are the Rass. God mentioned them in Surah Ya-Sin. It was also said: they are the people of the trench (al-Ukhdud), and al-Rass is the trench they dug. ʿIkrimah said: they are a people who buried their prophet alive in a well. The evidence for this is what:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The first of mankind to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection will be a black slave. That is because God sent a prophet to the people of a town, and none of its people believed in him except that black slave. Then the people of the town attacked that prophet, dug a well for him, threw him into it, and then closed it over him with a huge stone. That black slave used to go out to gather firewood, carrying it on his back, then bring his firewood and sell it, buying with it food and drink. Then he would come to that well, lift that stone, God helping him to do so, and lower to him his food and drink, then replace the stone as it was."

He said: This went on for as long as God willed. Then one day he went out to gather firewood as he usually did, gathered his wood, bound his bundle and finished it. When he wished to lift it, he felt drowsy, lay down and slept, and God struck his ear for seven years. Then he woke, stretched, turned onto his other side and lay down, and God struck his ear for another seven years. Then he woke, lifted his bundle, and supposed he had slept only an hour of the day. He came to the town, sold his bundle, bought food and drink as he used to, then went to the pit in its place, looking for it, but did not find it, for matters had changed among his people there. They took him out and believed in him and confirmed him.

He said: The Prophet used to ask them about that black slave, "What became of him?" They would say to him, "We do not know," until God took that prophet. Then God woke the black slave from his sleep, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "That black slave is truly the first to enter Paradise."

[Fath al-Qadir – al-Shawkani: 4/78.] [83]

I say: This hadith mentions that they believed in their prophet and brought him out of his pit, so they should not be the ones meant by His saying ﴿and the people of the Rass﴾, because God, exalted is He, informed about the people of the Rass that He destroyed them with destruction, unless they were destroyed for innovations they introduced after their prophet whom they brought out of the pit and believed in; in that case this would be a valid view.

It has been reported from Commander of the Faithful [Bihar al-Anwar: 14/149] ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, concerning the story of the people of the Rass, what confirms the statement of ʿIkrimah and his interpretation, and it is what:

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-ʿAbidin narrated from his father, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, that a man of the nobles of Banu Tamim, called ʿAmr, came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, inform me about the people of the Rass: in what era were they? Where were their dwellings? Who was their king? Did God send a messenger to them? And by what were they destroyed? For I find their mention in the Book of God, but I do not find their account." ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, said to him: "You have asked about a matter that no one before you has asked me about, and no one after me will tell you of it."

The account of them, O brother of Tamim, is that they were a people who worshipped a pine tree called Shah Darakht, which Yafith ibn Nuh had planted at the edge of a spring called Dushab, which had sprouted for Nuh, peace be upon him, after the Flood. They were called the people of the Rass because they buried their prophet in the earth, and that was before Sulayman ibn Dawud. They had twelve villages on the bank of a river called al-Rass in the lands of the East, and the river was named after them. In that time there was no more abundant or sweeter river on earth, nor villages with more inhabitants or more prosperous. Their greatest city was Isfandmah, where their king resided; he was called Nirkuz ibn ʿAnur ibn Nawash ibn Sarun ibn Nimrod ibn Kanʿan. In it were the spring and the pine tree. They had planted, in every village, a seed from the cone of that pine, and the seed sprouted and became a great tree. They forbade drinking from the spring and the rivers, so neither they nor their livestock drank from them, and whoever did so they killed. They said: "It is the life of our gods, so no one should pluck from its seeds." They and their livestock drank from the river al-Rass on which their villages stood. In every month of the year, in every village, they held a festival to which its people gathered, and they stretched over the tree a veil of silk bearing all kinds of images. Then they brought sheep and cattle and slaughtered them as offerings to the tree, and they set fire to them with wood. When the smoke of those sacrifices rose into the air and blocked their view of the sky, they fell prostrate before the tree, weeping and imploring it to be pleased with them.

Satan would come, shake its branches and cry out from its trunk like a child: "I am pleased with you, my servants, so be content and let your eyes be cool." Then they would raise their heads, drink wine and play instruments, remaining so for their day and night. Then they would disperse. When the festival of their greatest town came, its young and old gathered; they set up a pavilion beside the pine and the spring and offered to it sacrifices many times more than they had offered to the tree in their villages. Then Iblis would come, shake the pine violently, and speak from within it with a booming voice, promising them and offering them more than all the devils had promised. They would raise their heads from prostration, filled with such joy and vigour that they could not recover from drinking and music, and they would remain so for twelve days and nights, corresponding to the number of their festivals in the year, and then disperse.

When their disbelief in God and their worship of other than Him grew long, God sent to them a prophet from the Children of Israel, of the offspring of Judah son of Jacob. He stayed among them a long time, calling them to the worship of God, exalted is He, and to recognition of His lordship, but they did not follow him. When he saw their extreme persistence in error and misguidance, and their refusal to accept what he called them to of guidance and righteousness, and he came to their greatest town, he said: "O Lord, Your servants have refused anything but to deny me and to disbelieve in You, and they have taken to worshipping a tree that neither benefits nor harms. So wither their tree entirely, and show them Your power and authority." In the morning the people found their whole tree withered. This alarmed them and they were divided into two groups: one group said, "The sorcery of your gods has done this—this man who claims to be the messenger of the Lord of heaven and earth to you, in order to turn your faces from your gods toward his god."

Another group said, "No, rather your gods became angry when they saw this man disparaging them, reviling them, and calling you to worship other than them, so they withdrew their beauty and radiance so that you would become angry for them, and they would take vengeance on him." Their opinion was unanimously to kill him. They made long tubes of lead with wide mouths and sent them down into the bottom of the spring, one above another, like conduits. They drained the water within, then dug at its bottom a narrow, deep well, sent their prophet down into it, and stopped its mouth with a huge rock. Then they removed the tubes from the water and said: "We hope now that our gods will be pleased with us, since they have seen that we have killed the one who reviled them and turned people from their worship, and buried him beneath their greatest one, so that they may be healed of him and their light and splendour return as they were." They remained most of that day hearing the groaning of their prophet, peace be upon him, as he said: "My master, You see the narrowness of my place and the severity of my distress. Have mercy on my weakness and my lack of strength, hasten the taking of my soul, and do not delay the answer to my prayer," until he died, peace be upon him.

God, exalted is He, said to Jibril: "These servants of Mine have been deceived by My forbearance, felt secure from My plotting, worshipped other than Me, and killed My messenger. I am the avenger of those who disobey Me and do not fear My punishment, and I have sworn that I will make them an example and a warning to the worlds." They were not alarmed, while they were at their festival, except by a violent, fierce, deep-red wind, which stripped them bare and left them bewildered. They pressed together, and then the earth beneath them became a stone of sulphur blazing, and a black cloud overshadowed them and rained down upon them like a red, flaming dome, and their bodies melted as lead melts in fire. We seek refuge with God from His anger and the reach of His vengeance.

Some scholars of the accounts of past peoples and the biographies of earlier generations said: "I have been told that there were two Rass. As for one of them, its people were nomads, dwellers of tents, and herdsmen. God sent to them a messenger, and they killed him. Then He sent them another messenger and supported him with a saint (wali), and they killed the messenger, and the saint struggled against them until he silenced them. They used to say, 'Our god is in the sea,' and they were on its shore. Every month a devil would come out to them from the sea, and they would slaughter before it and make it a festival. The saint said to them, 'Do you see: if your god, whom you worship, came out, and I called upon him and he answered me and I commanded him and he obeyed me, would you respond to what I call you to?' They said, 'Yes.' So they gave him their covenants and pledges upon that. They waited until that devil came out in the form of a fish, riding four fish, with a long neck raised up and something like a crown on its head. When they looked at it, they fell down prostrate. The saint went out to it and said, 'Come to me willingly or unwillingly, in the name of God the Generous.' Then it descended from its fish and the saint said to it, 'Come to me upon them, so that there may be no doubt among the people about its matter.' It came, and they brought it, dragging it and being dragged by it, until they reached the shore. Then they denied him after that, so God sent a wind upon them which flung them into the sea, and it flung into the sea their livestock and what they possessed of gold, silver and vessels. The righteous saint went to the sea and took the gold, silver and vessels and divided them equally among his companions, and the line of these people was cut off."

"As for the other Rass: they were a people who had a river called al-Rass, after which they were named. There were many prophets among them; scarcely did a prophet arise among them without being killed. That river was at the far edge of Adharbayjan, between it and Armenia: if you crossed it going back you entered the bounds of Armenia, and if you crossed it coming forward you entered the bounds of Adharbayjan. Those around them from Armenia worshipped idols, and those in front of them from Adharbayjan worshipped fire. They worshipped virgin maidens, and when one of them reached thirty years, they killed her and substituted another.

The breadth of their river was three farsakhs, and it rose each day and night until it reached the middle of the mountains around it. It did not settle on land or sea: when it left their boundary it would stop, turn, and return to them. God sent to them thirty prophets in one month, and they killed them all. Then God sent to them a prophet, supported him with His help, and sent with him a saint; he struggled against them for God with the struggle due to Him, and they rejected him openly. God sent Mikail, and this was at the time the seed falls into the field, when they were most in need of water. He caused their river to burst into the sea, so that what was at its bottom drained away, and he came to its springs from above and blocked them up.

God sent His helpers from the angels, five hundred thousand, and they dispersed what remained in the middle of the river. Then God commanded Jibril, who descended and left in their land no spring, no water, no river, without drying it up by God's permission. He commanded the Angel of Death, who went to the livestock and caused them to die in a single instant. He commanded the four winds, the south, the north, the east and the west, and they shattered whatever goods they had. God cast sleep upon them; then the four winds swept away all those goods, scattering them over the mountain peaks and the valley bottoms. As for their ornaments, silver or gold, or vessels, God commanded the earth and it swallowed them. They woke with no livestock, no property to return to, and no water to drink, and their crops were withered. Then a few of them believed in God, and God guided them to a cave in a mountain that had a path leading behind it; they were saved. They numbered twenty-one men, four women and two children. The rest of the men, women and children numbered six hundred thousand, and they died of thirst and hunger, and none of them remained.

Then the believing people returned to their dwellings and found that their upper parts had become their lower parts. They called upon God then, sincerely, that He would bring them crops, livestock and water, and make it little so that they would not transgress. God answered them in this, knowing their sincerity, and released their river for them and gave them more than they had asked.

Those people remained in obedience to God, outwardly and inwardly, until they passed away. Then after them came a generation who obeyed God outwardly but were hypocrites inwardly, and God gave them respite. Then their disobedience multiplied, so God set their enemy over them, who swiftly slew them, and a remnant was left. God then sent the plague upon them, and not one of them remained. Their river and dwellings remained for two hundred years with no one living in them.

Then God brought after that a new generation, who settled there and were righteous for some years. Then they introduced a foul practice: a man would call his daughter, his sister and his wife, and his neighbour and friend and brother would have intercourse with her, seeking by that piety and kinship. Then they advanced from that to another kind, where a man was content with a man and they abandoned women until they became lustful. A female demon came to them in the form of a woman; she was Dalhath, daughter of Iblis, sister of Satan—they were in one egg—and she made the riding of women upon one another appear attractive to them and taught them how to do it. Thus the origin of women mounting one another is from Dalhath. God then sent upon that generation a thunderbolt at the beginning of the night, a sinking of the earth at the end of the night, and a cry at sunrise, and not one of them remained, and their dwellings were destroyed."

Part of this story is corroborated by what:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: al-Hasan ibn Ismaʿil al-Dinawari told us... — Ibn Fanjawayh said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik told us; al-Hasan ibn Ismaʿil al-Dinawari told us; Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Malik al-Susi told us; Nasr ibn Hammad told us; ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, from Makhul, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Among the signs of the Hour is that men will suffice themselves with men and women with women, and that is sahq."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Abu al-Tayyib ibn Hafsawayh told us; ʿAbd Allah ibn Jami' told us; ʿUthman ibn Kharzadh told us; Salman ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman told us; al-Hakam ibn Yaʿla ibn ʿAta' told us; Muʿawiyah ibn ʿAmmar al-Dahni told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, concerning His saying ﴿and the people of the Rass﴾, who said: "The sahqat" (women who practise sahq).

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/33.] [84]

Al-Rass in the language of the Arabs means every excavated thing, such as a well, a mine, a grave and the like, and its plural is risas. The poet said:

"I have outstripped to the front with people of Tanabilah... digging the risas."

[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 19/20.]

Abu Ubayd said: al-Rass is every well that has not been lined with stones, bricks or wood.

﴿And We destroyed many generations between them.﴾ And to each We set forth parables, establishing the proof; yet We destroyed them only after warning and admonition. ﴿And each We utterly destroyed with complete destruction.﴾ That is, We annihilated them with annihilation. The historian said: al-Akhfash said: We shattered them into pieces.

﴿And indeed they have passed by the town upon which a rain of evil was rained down.﴾ That is, the rain of stones. It was the town of the people of Lot, and there were five towns. Allah, glorified is He, destroyed four of them and the fifth remained. Its name was Sughar, and its people did not do that vile deed.

﴿Had they not been seeing it?﴾ when they passed by it on their journeys, so that they would take heed and be mindful. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Rather, they did not expect to be raised.﴾ That is, they did not fear resurrection.

﴿And when they see you, they take you only for mockery.﴾ It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl: whenever he passed by his companions while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was present, he would say mockingly: ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger? He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in them.﴾ He almost turned us away from their worship. ﴿And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in the way.﴾ This is a warning to them.

﴿Have you seen one who has taken his desire as his god?﴾ This is because a man among the polytheists would worship a stone or an idol; if he saw something better than it, he would throw it away and take the other and worship it. Ibn Abbas said: "Hawa (desire) is a god worshipped besides Allah."

﴿Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾ a protector, preventing him from going out into this corruption. It was abrogated by the verse of jihad.

﴿Or do you think that most of them hear?﴾ what he says, the hearing of one seeking understanding, ﴿or reason?﴾ what they witness of proofs and signs. ﴿They are only like livestock; rather, they are further astray in the way.﴾ Because animals find their way to their pastures and watering places, and submit to their owners who feed and care for them, whereas these disbelievers do not recognize the path of truth and do not obey their Lord who created and provided for them.

﴿Have you not seen your Lord, how He extends the shade?﴾ Its meaning: have you not seen the extension of your Lord's shade? It is what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun. He made it extended because there is no sun with it, as He said of the shade of Paradise: ﴿and extended shade﴾, since there was no sun in it. ﴿And had He willed, He would have made it still, constant and fixed, not moving and not removed by the sun.﴾

Abu Ubayd said: the shade (zill) is what the sun has cancelled, and it is in the morning; and the fay' is what the sun has cancelled after its decline (zawal), and it was named fay' because it moves from the side of the east to the side of the west.

﴿Then We made the sun over it,﴾ that is, over the shade, ﴿an indicator.﴾ The meaning of its indicating it is that if there were no sun, the shade would not be known, since things are known by their opposites. The shade follows the sun in its lengthening and shortening, as the traveller follows the guide. When the sun rises, the shade shortens, and when it sinks, the shade lengthens. ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal.﴾ That is, the shade, by the sun that comes and cancels it. The meaning of His words "gradual" is light and swift. The word "qabd" means gathering scattered parts, and here it means a gentle transfer.

﴿And it is He who made the night for you as a garment,﴾ that is, a covering in which you conceal yourselves and rest. ﴿And sleep as rest,﴾ a repose for your bodies and a cessation of your labour. The root of sabt is cutting off, from which comes the day of Saturday (sabt) and sabtiyya sandals. ﴿And made the day a resurrection,﴾ that is, an awakening and life, in which you rise up and scatter for your affairs.

﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water,﴾ that is, pure in itself and purifying for others, ﴿that We may give life thereby to a dead land,﴾ "dead" is used rather than "dead (feminine)" because it refers to the place and the locality. Ka'b said: "Rain is the spirit of the earth." ﴿And that We may give it to drink﴾ — the common readers recite it with a dammed nun, while al-Mufaddal and al-Barjami narrated from Asim with a fatha on the nun, which is the reading of the Commander of the Faithful Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) — ﴿of what We have created, cattle and many people.﴾ Al-anasi is the plural of al-insan (human being); its original form was anasin, like bustan and basatin, and the ba' was substituted for the nun. It is also said to be a valid form, just as qarqur becomes qarariq and qarāqir.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Fanjawi informed me, saying: Makhlad ibn Ja'far al-Baqirhi narrated to us; al-Hasan ibn Alawi narrated to us; Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Juraij and Muqatil all said, and they traced it back to Ibn Mas'ud: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No year is more abundant in rain than another; rather, Allah distributes these provisions and places them in the lowest heaven in this rain, which descends each year in a known measure and known weight. But when a people commit sins, Allah diverts it to others; and when they all disobey, Allah diverts it to the deserts and the seas." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/57, with variation.] [85]

﴿And We have indeed distributed it among them,﴾ that is, the rain, ﴿year after year, and in one town rather than another.﴾ It is also said: We distributed it among them as heavy rain, drizzle, showers and fine mist. It is also said: the distribution refers to the wind.

﴿So that they may take heed, yet most people refused except disbelief,﴾ that is, denial. It is also said: it is their saying "such-and-such rain." ﴿And had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town,﴾ a messenger, and We would have distributed the warner among them just as We distributed the rain. In that case the burden of prophethood would be lighter on you, but We have laid upon you the weight of warning all the towns, so that by your patience in it you may merit what We have prepared for you of honour, dignity and high rank.

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers﴾ in what they call you to of worshipping their gods, approaching them, or flattering them, ﴿and strive against them with it﴾ — that is, with the Qur'an — ﴿a great striving.﴾

And We certainly gave Musa the Book and appointed with him his brother Harun as a minister (wazir), meaning a helper and supporter. Then We said: "Go to the people who denied Our signs", meaning the Copts. In the verse there is an omitted element which is understood from the context, its estimated form being: so they denied both of them.
Then We destroyed them with complete destruction, meaning We annihilated them with total annihilation. And the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind, an admonition. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers in the Hereafter a painful punishment, in addition to the punishment that had already befallen them in this world.

As for ʿĀd and Thamud and the People of the Rass (al-Rass, the well), they have been disputed. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they were people of wells. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: they were the people of a well, sitting beside it, and they were herdsmen; they worshipped idols. God sent to them Shuʿayb, calling them to Islam. He came to them and invited them, but they persisted in their rebellion and in harming Shuʿayb, so God warned them of His punishment. While they were around the well in their dwellings, the well collapsed, swallowing them together with their homes and their possessions, and they all perished.

Qatadah said: al-Rass is a village in Falj al-Yamamah. They killed their prophet, so God destroyed them. Some of them said: they were the remnant of the people of Hud and the people of Salih, and they are the people of the well which God mentions in His saying: ﴿And a deserted well and a lofty palace﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 45].

Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn al-Kalbi and al-Khalil said: they had a prophet called Hanzalah ibn Safwan. In their land there was a mountain called Fatah, whose summit rose a mile into the sky. The ʿanqa' (a mythical bird) used to frequent it; it was the largest of birds and had every colour. They named it ʿanqa' because of the length of its neck. It would dwell on that mountain and swoop down on birds to eat them. One day it grew hungry, and birds were scarce, so it swooped on a child and carried him off. For this reason it was named ʿanqa' Maghrib, because it disappears (yaghrib) with what it takes and carries it away. Then it swooped on a girl once she had grown up, seized her and pressed her to its two small wings, apart from its two large wings, and flew away with her. They complained to their prophet, and he said: "O God, seize it and cut off its offspring." A thunderbolt struck it and it burned, leaving no trace. The Arabs mentioned it in their poetry. Then they killed their prophet, and God destroyed them.

Ka'b, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: they are the people of Ya-Sin, and al-Rass is a well at Antioch in which they killed Habib the carpenter; they were attributed to it, and they are the Rass. God mentioned them in Surah Ya-Sin. It was also said: they are the people of the trench (al-Ukhdud), and al-Rass is the trench they dug. ʿIkrimah said: they are a people who buried their prophet alive in a well. The evidence for this is what:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The first of mankind to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection will be a black slave. That is because God sent a prophet to the people of a town, and none of its people believed in him except that black slave. Then the people of the town attacked that prophet, dug a well for him, threw him into it, and then closed it over him with a huge stone. That black slave used to go out to gather firewood, carrying it on his back, then bring his firewood and sell it, buying with it food and drink. Then he would come to that well, lift that stone, God helping him to do so, and lower to him his food and drink, then replace the stone as it was."

He said: This went on for as long as God willed. Then one day he went out to gather firewood as he usually did, gathered his wood, bound his bundle and finished it. When he wished to lift it, he felt drowsy, lay down and slept, and God struck his ear for seven years. Then he woke, stretched, turned onto his other side and lay down, and God struck his ear for another seven years. Then he woke, lifted his bundle, and supposed he had slept only an hour of the day. He came to the town, sold his bundle, bought food and drink as he used to, then went to the pit in its place, looking for it, but did not find it, for matters had changed among his people there. They took him out and believed in him and confirmed him.

He said: The Prophet used to ask them about that black slave, "What became of him?" They would say to him, "We do not know," until God took that prophet. Then God woke the black slave from his sleep, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "That black slave is truly the first to enter Paradise."

[Fath al-Qadir – al-Shawkani: 4/78.] [83]

I say: This hadith mentions that they believed in their prophet and brought him out of his pit, so they should not be the ones meant by His saying ﴿and the people of the Rass﴾, because God, exalted is He, informed about the people of the Rass that He destroyed them with destruction, unless they were destroyed for innovations they introduced after their prophet whom they brought out of the pit and believed in; in that case this would be a valid view.

It has been reported from Commander of the Faithful [Bihar al-Anwar: 14/149] ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, concerning the story of the people of the Rass, what confirms the statement of ʿIkrimah and his interpretation, and it is what:

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-ʿAbidin narrated from his father, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, that a man of the nobles of Banu Tamim, called ʿAmr, came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, inform me about the people of the Rass: in what era were they? Where were their dwellings? Who was their king? Did God send a messenger to them? And by what were they destroyed? For I find their mention in the Book of God, but I do not find their account." ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, said to him: "You have asked about a matter that no one before you has asked me about, and no one after me will tell you of it."

The account of them, O brother of Tamim, is that they were a people who worshipped a pine tree called Shah Darakht, which Yafith ibn Nuh had planted at the edge of a spring called Dushab, which had sprouted for Nuh, peace be upon him, after the Flood. They were called the people of the Rass because they buried their prophet in the earth, and that was before Sulayman ibn Dawud. They had twelve villages on the bank of a river called al-Rass in the lands of the East, and the river was named after them. In that time there was no more abundant or sweeter river on earth, nor villages with more inhabitants or more prosperous. Their greatest city was Isfandmah, where their king resided; he was called Nirkuz ibn ʿAnur ibn Nawash ibn Sarun ibn Nimrod ibn Kanʿan. In it were the spring and the pine tree. They had planted, in every village, a seed from the cone of that pine, and the seed sprouted and became a great tree. They forbade drinking from the spring and the rivers, so neither they nor their livestock drank from them, and whoever did so they killed. They said: "It is the life of our gods, so no one should pluck from its seeds." They and their livestock drank from the river al-Rass on which their villages stood. In every month of the year, in every village, they held a festival to which its people gathered, and they stretched over the tree a veil of silk bearing all kinds of images. Then they brought sheep and cattle and slaughtered them as offerings to the tree, and they set fire to them with wood. When the smoke of those sacrifices rose into the air and blocked their view of the sky, they fell prostrate before the tree, weeping and imploring it to be pleased with them.

Satan would come, shake its branches and cry out from its trunk like a child: "I am pleased with you, my servants, so be content and let your eyes be cool." Then they would raise their heads, drink wine and play instruments, remaining so for their day and night. Then they would disperse. When the festival of their greatest town came, its young and old gathered; they set up a pavilion beside the pine and the spring and offered to it sacrifices many times more than they had offered to the tree in their villages. Then Iblis would come, shake the pine violently, and speak from within it with a booming voice, promising them and offering them more than all the devils had promised. They would raise their heads from prostration, filled with such joy and vigour that they could not recover from drinking and music, and they would remain so for twelve days and nights, corresponding to the number of their festivals in the year, and then disperse.

When their disbelief in God and their worship of other than Him grew long, God sent to them a prophet from the Children of Israel, of the offspring of Judah son of Jacob. He stayed among them a long time, calling them to the worship of God, exalted is He, and to recognition of His lordship, but they did not follow him. When he saw their extreme persistence in error and misguidance, and their refusal to accept what he called them to of guidance and righteousness, and he came to their greatest town, he said: "O Lord, Your servants have refused anything but to deny me and to disbelieve in You, and they have taken to worshipping a tree that neither benefits nor harms. So wither their tree entirely, and show them Your power and authority." In the morning the people found their whole tree withered. This alarmed them and they were divided into two groups: one group said, "The sorcery of your gods has done this—this man who claims to be the messenger of the Lord of heaven and earth to you, in order to turn your faces from your gods toward his god."

Another group said, "No, rather your gods became angry when they saw this man disparaging them, reviling them, and calling you to worship other than them, so they withdrew their beauty and radiance so that you would become angry for them, and they would take vengeance on him." Their opinion was unanimously to kill him. They made long tubes of lead with wide mouths and sent them down into the bottom of the spring, one above another, like conduits. They drained the water within, then dug at its bottom a narrow, deep well, sent their prophet down into it, and stopped its mouth with a huge rock. Then they removed the tubes from the water and said: "We hope now that our gods will be pleased with us, since they have seen that we have killed the one who reviled them and turned people from their worship, and buried him beneath their greatest one, so that they may be healed of him and their light and splendour return as they were." They remained most of that day hearing the groaning of their prophet, peace be upon him, as he said: "My master, You see the narrowness of my place and the severity of my distress. Have mercy on my weakness and my lack of strength, hasten the taking of my soul, and do not delay the answer to my prayer," until he died, peace be upon him.

God, exalted is He, said to Jibril: "These servants of Mine have been deceived by My forbearance, felt secure from My plotting, worshipped other than Me, and killed My messenger. I am the avenger of those who disobey Me and do not fear My punishment, and I have sworn that I will make them an example and a warning to the worlds." They were not alarmed, while they were at their festival, except by a violent, fierce, deep-red wind, which stripped them bare and left them bewildered. They pressed together, and then the earth beneath them became a stone of sulphur blazing, and a black cloud overshadowed them and rained down upon them like a red, flaming dome, and their bodies melted as lead melts in fire. We seek refuge with God from His anger and the reach of His vengeance.

Some scholars of the accounts of past peoples and the biographies of earlier generations said: "I have been told that there were two Rass. As for one of them, its people were nomads, dwellers of tents, and herdsmen. God sent to them a messenger, and they killed him. Then He sent them another messenger and supported him with a saint (wali), and they killed the messenger, and the saint struggled against them until he silenced them. They used to say, 'Our god is in the sea,' and they were on its shore. Every month a devil would come out to them from the sea, and they would slaughter before it and make it a festival. The saint said to them, 'Do you see: if your god, whom you worship, came out, and I called upon him and he answered me and I commanded him and he obeyed me, would you respond to what I call you to?' They said, 'Yes.' So they gave him their covenants and pledges upon that. They waited until that devil came out in the form of a fish, riding four fish, with a long neck raised up and something like a crown on its head. When they looked at it, they fell down prostrate. The saint went out to it and said, 'Come to me willingly or unwillingly, in the name of God the Generous.' Then it descended from its fish and the saint said to it, 'Come to me upon them, so that there may be no doubt among the people about its matter.' It came, and they brought it, dragging it and being dragged by it, until they reached the shore. Then they denied him after that, so God sent a wind upon them which flung them into the sea, and it flung into the sea their livestock and what they possessed of gold, silver and vessels. The righteous saint went to the sea and took the gold, silver and vessels and divided them equally among his companions, and the line of these people was cut off."

"As for the other Rass: they were a people who had a river called al-Rass, after which they were named. There were many prophets among them; scarcely did a prophet arise among them without being killed. That river was at the far edge of Adharbayjan, between it and Armenia: if you crossed it going back you entered the bounds of Armenia, and if you crossed it coming forward you entered the bounds of Adharbayjan. Those around them from Armenia worshipped idols, and those in front of them from Adharbayjan worshipped fire. They worshipped virgin maidens, and when one of them reached thirty years, they killed her and substituted another.

The breadth of their river was three farsakhs, and it rose each day and night until it reached the middle of the mountains around it. It did not settle on land or sea: when it left their boundary it would stop, turn, and return to them. God sent to them thirty prophets in one month, and they killed them all. Then God sent to them a prophet, supported him with His help, and sent with him a saint; he struggled against them for God with the struggle due to Him, and they rejected him openly. God sent Mikail, and this was at the time the seed falls into the field, when they were most in need of water. He caused their river to burst into the sea, so that what was at its bottom drained away, and he came to its springs from above and blocked them up.

God sent His helpers from the angels, five hundred thousand, and they dispersed what remained in the middle of the river. Then God commanded Jibril, who descended and left in their land no spring, no water, no river, without drying it up by God's permission. He commanded the Angel of Death, who went to the livestock and caused them to die in a single instant. He commanded the four winds, the south, the north, the east and the west, and they shattered whatever goods they had. God cast sleep upon them; then the four winds swept away all those goods, scattering them over the mountain peaks and the valley bottoms. As for their ornaments, silver or gold, or vessels, God commanded the earth and it swallowed them. They woke with no livestock, no property to return to, and no water to drink, and their crops were withered. Then a few of them believed in God, and God guided them to a cave in a mountain that had a path leading behind it; they were saved. They numbered twenty-one men, four women and two children. The rest of the men, women and children numbered six hundred thousand, and they died of thirst and hunger, and none of them remained.

Then the believing people returned to their dwellings and found that their upper parts had become their lower parts. They called upon God then, sincerely, that He would bring them crops, livestock and water, and make it little so that they would not transgress. God answered them in this, knowing their sincerity, and released their river for them and gave them more than they had asked.

Those people remained in obedience to God, outwardly and inwardly, until they passed away. Then after them came a generation who obeyed God outwardly but were hypocrites inwardly, and God gave them respite. Then their disobedience multiplied, so God set their enemy over them, who swiftly slew them, and a remnant was left. God then sent the plague upon them, and not one of them remained. Their river and dwellings remained for two hundred years with no one living in them.

Then God brought after that a new generation, who settled there and were righteous for some years. Then they introduced a foul practice: a man would call his daughter, his sister and his wife, and his neighbour and friend and brother would have intercourse with her, seeking by that piety and kinship. Then they advanced from that to another kind, where a man was content with a man and they abandoned women until they became lustful. A female demon came to them in the form of a woman; she was Dalhath, daughter of Iblis, sister of Satan—they were in one egg—and she made the riding of women upon one another appear attractive to them and taught them how to do it. Thus the origin of women mounting one another is from Dalhath. God then sent upon that generation a thunderbolt at the beginning of the night, a sinking of the earth at the end of the night, and a cry at sunrise, and not one of them remained, and their dwellings were destroyed."

Part of this story is corroborated by what:

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: al-Hasan ibn Ismaʿil al-Dinawari told us... — Ibn Fanjawayh said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik told us; al-Hasan ibn Ismaʿil al-Dinawari told us; Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Malik al-Susi told us; Nasr ibn Hammad told us; ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, from Makhul, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Among the signs of the Hour is that men will suffice themselves with men and women with women, and that is sahq."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Abu al-Tayyib ibn Hafsawayh told us; ʿAbd Allah ibn Jami' told us; ʿUthman ibn Kharzadh told us; Salman ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman told us; al-Hakam ibn Yaʿla ibn ʿAta' told us; Muʿawiyah ibn ʿAmmar al-Dahni told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, concerning His saying ﴿and the people of the Rass﴾, who said: "The sahqat" (women who practise sahq).

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/33.] [84]

Al-Rass in the language of the Arabs means every excavated thing, such as a well, a mine, a grave and the like, and its plural is risas. The poet said:

"I have outstripped to the front with people of Tanabilah... digging the risas."

[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 19/20.]

Abu Ubayd said: al-Rass is every well that has not been lined with stones, bricks or wood.

﴿And We destroyed many generations between them.﴾ And to each We set forth parables, establishing the proof; yet We destroyed them only after warning and admonition. ﴿And each We utterly destroyed with complete destruction.﴾ That is, We annihilated them with annihilation. The historian said: al-Akhfash said: We shattered them into pieces.

﴿And indeed they have passed by the town upon which a rain of evil was rained down.﴾ That is, the rain of stones. It was the town of the people of Lot, and there were five towns. Allah, glorified is He, destroyed four of them and the fifth remained. Its name was Sughar, and its people did not do that vile deed.

﴿Had they not been seeing it?﴾ when they passed by it on their journeys, so that they would take heed and be mindful. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Rather, they did not expect to be raised.﴾ That is, they did not fear resurrection.

﴿And when they see you, they take you only for mockery.﴾ It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl: whenever he passed by his companions while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was present, he would say mockingly: ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger? He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in them.﴾ He almost turned us away from their worship. ﴿And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in the way.﴾ This is a warning to them.

﴿Have you seen one who has taken his desire as his god?﴾ This is because a man among the polytheists would worship a stone or an idol; if he saw something better than it, he would throw it away and take the other and worship it. Ibn Abbas said: "Hawa (desire) is a god worshipped besides Allah."

﴿Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾ a protector, preventing him from going out into this corruption. It was abrogated by the verse of jihad.

﴿Or do you think that most of them hear?﴾ what he says, the hearing of one seeking understanding, ﴿or reason?﴾ what they witness of proofs and signs. ﴿They are only like livestock; rather, they are further astray in the way.﴾ Because animals find their way to their pastures and watering places, and submit to their owners who feed and care for them, whereas these disbelievers do not recognize the path of truth and do not obey their Lord who created and provided for them.

﴿Have you not seen your Lord, how He extends the shade?﴾ Its meaning: have you not seen the extension of your Lord's shade? It is what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun. He made it extended because there is no sun with it, as He said of the shade of Paradise: ﴿and extended shade﴾, since there was no sun in it. ﴿And had He willed, He would have made it still, constant and fixed, not moving and not removed by the sun.﴾

Abu Ubayd said: the shade (zill) is what the sun has cancelled, and it is in the morning; and the fay' is what the sun has cancelled after its decline (zawal), and it was named fay' because it moves from the side of the east to the side of the west.

﴿Then We made the sun over it,﴾ that is, over the shade, ﴿an indicator.﴾ The meaning of its indicating it is that if there were no sun, the shade would not be known, since things are known by their opposites. The shade follows the sun in its lengthening and shortening, as the traveller follows the guide. When the sun rises, the shade shortens, and when it sinks, the shade lengthens. ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal.﴾ That is, the shade, by the sun that comes and cancels it. The meaning of His words "gradual" is light and swift. The word "qabd" means gathering scattered parts, and here it means a gentle transfer.

﴿And it is He who made the night for you as a garment,﴾ that is, a covering in which you conceal yourselves and rest. ﴿And sleep as rest,﴾ a repose for your bodies and a cessation of your labour. The root of sabt is cutting off, from which comes the day of Saturday (sabt) and sabtiyya sandals. ﴿And made the day a resurrection,﴾ that is, an awakening and life, in which you rise up and scatter for your affairs.

﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water,﴾ that is, pure in itself and purifying for others, ﴿that We may give life thereby to a dead land,﴾ "dead" is used rather than "dead (feminine)" because it refers to the place and the locality. Ka'b said: "Rain is the spirit of the earth." ﴿And that We may give it to drink﴾ — the common readers recite it with a dammed nun, while al-Mufaddal and al-Barjami narrated from Asim with a fatha on the nun, which is the reading of the Commander of the Faithful Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) — ﴿of what We have created, cattle and many people.﴾ Al-anasi is the plural of al-insan (human being); its original form was anasin, like bustan and basatin, and the ba' was substituted for the nun. It is also said to be a valid form, just as qarqur becomes qarariq and qarāqir.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Fanjawi informed me, saying: Makhlad ibn Ja'far al-Baqirhi narrated to us; al-Hasan ibn Alawi narrated to us; Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Juraij and Muqatil all said, and they traced it back to Ibn Mas'ud: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No year is more abundant in rain than another; rather, Allah distributes these provisions and places them in the lowest heaven in this rain, which descends each year in a known measure and known weight. But when a people commit sins, Allah diverts it to others; and when they all disobey, Allah diverts it to the deserts and the seas." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/57, with variation.] [85]

﴿And We have indeed distributed it among them,﴾ that is, the rain, ﴿year after year, and in one town rather than another.﴾ It is also said: We distributed it among them as heavy rain, drizzle, showers and fine mist. It is also said: the distribution refers to the wind.

﴿So that they may take heed, yet most people refused except disbelief,﴾ that is, denial. It is also said: it is their saying "such-and-such rain." ﴿And had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town,﴾ a messenger, and We would have distributed the warner among them just as We distributed the rain. In that case the burden of prophethood would be lighter on you, but We have laid upon you the weight of warning all the towns, so that by your patience in it you may merit what We have prepared for you of honour, dignity and high rank.

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers﴾ in what they call you to of worshipping their gods, approaching them, or flattering them, ﴿and strive against them with it﴾ — that is, with the Qur'an — ﴿a great striving.﴾

And We certainly gave Musa the Book and appointed with him his brother Harun as a minister (wazir), meaning a helper and supporter. Then We said: "Go to the people who denied Our signs", meaning the Copts. In the verse there is an omitted element which is understood from the context, its estimated form being: so they denied both of them.
Then We destroyed them with complete destruction, meaning We annihilated them with total annihilation. And the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind, an admonition. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers in the Hereafter a painful punishment, in addition to the punishment that had already befallen them in this world.

As for ʿĀd and Thamud and the People of the Rass (al-Rass, the well), they have been disputed. Ibn ʿAbbas said: they were people of wells. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: they were the people of a well, sitting beside it, and they were herdsmen; they worshipped idols. God sent to them Shuʿayb, calling them to Islam. He came to them and invited them, but they persisted in their rebellion and in harming Shuʿayb, so God warned them of His punishment. While they were around the well in their dwellings, the well collapsed, swallowing them together with their homes and their possessions, and they all perished.

Qatadah said: al-Rass is a village in Falj al-Yamamah. They killed their prophet, so God destroyed them. Some of them said: they were the remnant of the people of Hud and the people of Salih, and they are the people of the well which God mentions in His saying: ﴿And a deserted well and a lofty palace﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 45].

Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn al-Kalbi and al-Khalil said: they had a prophet called Hanzalah ibn Safwan. In their land there was a mountain called Fatah, whose summit rose a mile into the sky. The ʿanqa' (a mythical bird) used to frequent it; it was the largest of birds and had every colour. They named it ʿanqa' because of the length of its neck. It would dwell on that mountain and swoop down on birds to eat them. One day it grew hungry, and birds were scarce, so it swooped on a child and carried him off. For this reason it was named ʿanqa' Maghrib, because it disappears (yaghrib) with what it takes and carries it away. Then it swooped on a girl once she had grown up, seized her and pressed her to its two small wings, apart from its two large wings, and flew away with her. They complained to their prophet, and he said: "O God, seize it and cut off its offspring." A thunderbolt struck it and it burned, leaving no trace. The Arabs mentioned it in their poetry. Then they killed their prophet, and God destroyed them.

Ka'b, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: they are the people of Ya-Sin, and al-Rass is a well at Antioch in which they killed Habib the carpenter; they were attributed to it, and they are the Rass. God mentioned them in Surah Ya-Sin. It was also said: they are the people of the trench (al-Ukhdud), and al-Rass is the trench they dug. ʿIkrimah said: they are a people who buried their prophet alive in a well. The evidence for this is what:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The first of mankind to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection will be a black slave. That is because God sent a prophet to the people of a town, and none of its people believed in him except that black slave. Then the people of the town attacked that prophet, dug a well for him, threw him into it, and then closed it over him with a huge stone. That black slave used to go out to gather firewood, carrying it on his back, then bring his firewood and sell it, buying with it food and drink. Then he would come to that well, lift that stone, God helping him to do so, and lower to him his food and drink, then replace the stone as it was."

He said: This went on for as long as God willed. Then one day he went out to gather firewood as he usually did, gathered his wood, bound his bundle and finished it. When he wished to lift it, he felt drowsy, lay down and slept, and God struck his ear for seven years. Then he woke, stretched, turned onto his other side and lay down, and God struck his ear for another seven years. Then he woke, lifted his bundle, and supposed he had slept only an hour of the day. He came to the town, sold his bundle, bought food and drink as he used to, then went to the pit in its place, looking for it, but did not find it, for matters had changed among his people there. They took him out and believed in him and confirmed him.

He said: The Prophet used to ask them about that black slave, "What became of him?" They would say to him, "We do not know," until God took that prophet. Then God woke the black slave from his sleep, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "That black slave is truly the first to enter Paradise."

[Fath al-Qadir – al-Shawkani: 4/78.] [83]

I say: This hadith mentions that they believed in their prophet and brought him out of his pit, so they should not be the ones meant by His saying ﴿and the people of the Rass﴾, because God, exalted is He, informed about the people of the Rass that He destroyed them with destruction, unless they were destroyed for innovations they introduced after their prophet whom they brought out of the pit and believed in; in that case this would be a valid view.

It has been reported from Commander of the Faithful [Bihar al-Anwar: 14/149] ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, concerning the story of the people of the Rass, what confirms the statement of ʿIkrimah and his interpretation, and it is what:

ʿAli ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-ʿAbidin narrated from his father, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, that a man of the nobles of Banu Tamim, called ʿAmr, came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, inform me about the people of the Rass: in what era were they? Where were their dwellings? Who was their king? Did God send a messenger to them? And by what were they destroyed? For I find their mention in the Book of God, but I do not find their account." ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, said to him: "You have asked about a matter that no one before you has asked me about, and no one after me will tell you of it."

The account of them, O brother of Tamim, is that they were a people who worshipped a pine tree called Shah Darakht, which Yafith ibn Nuh had planted at the edge of a spring called Dushab, which had sprouted for Nuh, peace be upon him, after the Flood. They were called the people of the Rass because they buried their prophet in the earth, and that was before Sulayman ibn Dawud. They had twelve villages on the bank of a river called al-Rass in the lands of the East, and the river was named after them. In that time there was no more abundant or sweeter river on earth, nor villages with more inhabitants or more prosperous. Their greatest city was Isfandmah, where their king resided; he was called Nirkuz ibn ʿAnur ibn Nawash ibn Sarun ibn Nimrod ibn Kanʿan. In it were the spring and the pine tree. They had planted, in every village, a seed from the cone of that pine, and the seed sprouted and became a great tree. They forbade drinking from the spring and the rivers, so neither they nor their livestock drank from them, and whoever did so they killed. They said: "It is the life of our gods, so no one should pluck from its seeds." They and their livestock drank from the river al-Rass on which their villages stood. In every month of the year, in every village, they held a festival to which its people gathered, and they stretched over the tree a veil of silk bearing all kinds of images. Then they brought sheep and cattle and slaughtered them as offerings to the tree, and they set fire to them with wood. When the smoke of those sacrifices rose into the air and blocked their view of the sky, they fell prostrate before the tree, weeping and imploring it to be pleased with them.

Satan would come, shake its branches and cry out from its trunk like a child: "I am pleased with you, my servants, so be content and let your eyes be cool." Then they would raise their heads, drink wine and play instruments, remaining so for their day and night. Then they would disperse. When the festival of their greatest town came, its young and old gathered; they set up a pavilion beside the pine and the spring and offered to it sacrifices many times more than they had offered to the tree in their villages. Then Iblis would come, shake the pine violently, and speak from within it with a booming voice, promising them and offering them more than all the devils had promised. They would raise their heads from prostration, filled with such joy and vigour that they could not recover from drinking and music, and they would remain so for twelve days and nights, corresponding to the number of their festivals in the year, and then disperse.

When their disbelief in God and their worship of other than Him grew long, God sent to them a prophet from the Children of Israel, of the offspring of Judah son of Jacob. He stayed among them a long time, calling them to the worship of God, exalted is He, and to recognition of His lordship, but they did not follow him. When he saw their extreme persistence in error and misguidance, and their refusal to accept what he called them to of guidance and righteousness, and he came to their greatest town, he said: "O Lord, Your servants have refused anything but to deny me and to disbelieve in You, and they have taken to worshipping a tree that neither benefits nor harms. So wither their tree entirely, and show them Your power and authority." In the morning the people found their whole tree withered. This alarmed them and they were divided into two groups: one group said, "The sorcery of your gods has done this—this man who claims to be the messenger of the Lord of heaven and earth to you, in order to turn your faces from your gods toward his god."

Another group said, "No, rather your gods became angry when they saw this man disparaging them, reviling them, and calling you to worship other than them, so they withdrew their beauty and radiance so that you would become angry for them, and they would take vengeance on him." Their opinion was unanimously to kill him. They made long tubes of lead with wide mouths and sent them down into the bottom of the spring, one above another, like conduits. They drained the water within, then dug at its bottom a narrow, deep well, sent their prophet down into it, and stopped its mouth with a huge rock.
