Shall we prostrate to what you command us?"﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited *ya'muruna* with a *ya'* (meaning: to what they command us), while others recited *ta'muruna* with a *ta'* (meaning: to what you command us, O Muhammad). ﴿And it increased them in aversion﴾, meaning the saying of the one who said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," increased them in aversion from the religion and faith. Sufyan al-Thawri, when he recited this verse, would raise his head to the sky and say: "My God, You have increased me in humility; may Your enemies' aversion not increase."

﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾, meaning the stations of the seven wandering planets. They are twelve constellations: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces. Aries and Scorpio are the houses of Mars; Taurus and Libra are the houses of Venus; Gemini and Virgo are the houses of Mercury; Cancer is the house of the Moon; Leo is the house of the Sun; Sagittarius and Pisces are the houses of Jupiter; Capricorn and Aquarius are the houses of Saturn. These constellations are divided among the four elements, so each of them has three constellations called the *muthallathat* (triplicities). Aries, Leo and Sagittarius are the fiery triplicity; Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn are the earthy triplicity; Gemini, Libra and Aquarius are the airy triplicity; Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces are the watery triplicity. The opinions of the commentators differ regarding the interpretation of *burudj* (constellations).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Shaykh narrated to me, saying: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from 'Ata' al-'Awfi, concerning the word of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾, that he said: "Palaces in which there are guards." Its evidence is His word: ﴿And even if you were in towers well-built﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 78.]].

Al-Akhtal said:

*As if it were a Roman tower, built by a builder with plaster, bricks and stones.*

Mujahid and Qatadah said: they are the stars.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Mahan narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, saying: my maternal uncle Ya'la narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, concerning ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾, that he said: "The great stars." 'Ata' said: they are the *sharaj*, which are the gates of the sky, called the Milky Way.

﴿And placed therein a lamp﴾, meaning the sun, similar to His word: ﴿And made the sun a lamp﴾ [[Surah Nuh: 16.]]. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited (*wa-ja'ala fiha suruja*) in the plural, meaning the stars, and this is the reading of the companions of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud). ﴿And a moon giving light﴾.

﴿And He it is who made the night and the day in succession﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning a replacement and a successor, one standing in place of the other, so whoever misses his deed in one of them makes it up in the other.

Qatadah said: "Show Allah good deeds in this night and day, for they are two steeds that carry people to their terms, that bring near everything far away, that wear out everything new, and that bring every promised thing to the Day of Resurrection."

Shamir [in the second copy: Shams] ibn 'Atiyyah narrated from Shaqiq, who said: A man came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "I missed the prayer last night." He said: "Make up what you missed of your night in your day, for Allah, the Exalted, made the night and the day in succession for whoever wishes to take heed."

Mujahid said: meaning He made each of them contrary to the other: this one black and that one white.

Ibn Zayd and others said: meaning one succeeds the other; when one goes, the other comes. They alternate in light and darkness, in increase and decrease. The following verse of Zuhayr supports this interpretation:

*In them the gazelles and the cows walk in succession, and their young ones rise from every bent-legged one.*

Muqatil said: meaning He made the day a successor to the night for whoever sleeps at night, and made the night a successor to the day for whoever has a need or is occupied.

﴿For whoever wishes to take heed﴾. The common readers recite it with a doubled *dhal*, meaning he remembers and admonishes himself. Hamzah and Khalaf recite it with a single *dhal*, from *dhikr* (remembrance). ﴿Or wishes gratitude﴾, meaning gratitude for the blessing of Allah, the Exalted, upon him.

﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful﴾, meaning the excellent servants. It is said this idiom (of *'ibad*) is for specification and distinction. Al-Hasan recited: *wa-'ubayd al-Rahman*.

﴿Those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾, meaning with tranquillity, dignity, obedience and humility, not arrogant, not exultant, not haughty, and not corrupters.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Qawhar informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi 'Isa narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Hushaym ibn 'Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His word, the Exalted, ﴿walk upon the earth in humility﴾, that he said: "Forbearance and knowledge." Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "They are people of dignity and chastity who do not behave foolishly; and if foolishness is directed at them, they show forbearance."

Al-Dahhak said: "Pious and chaste people who do not act ignorantly." He said: and it is in Syriac. Al-Thumali said: it is in Nabataean. The word *hawn* in the language means gentleness and softness, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Love your beloved gently, for he may one day become your enemy; and hate your enemy gently, for he may one day become your beloved." [[Al-Musannaf, al-San'ani: 11/181.]].

﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"﴾, meaning words of soundness, from Mujahid.

Ibn Hayyan said: words by which they are safe from sin.

Al-Hasan said: they greet them with peace. Its evidence is His word: ﴿And when they hear vain speech, they turn away from it and say, "To us are our deeds and to you are your deeds; peace be upon you"﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 55.]].

Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Kalbi said: this was before they were commanded to fight; then the verse of fighting abrogated it.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash, the reciter, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih [al-Kaylisi] [[So in the manuscript.]] narrated to us in Makkah, saying: Salamah ibn Shabib [in the second copy: Shu'ayb] narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Shaybān ibn Mihran narrated to us, from Khalid ibn al-Mughirah ibn Qays, from Abu Mihlaz Lahiq ibn Humayd, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "I have seen people from my community who have not yet been created, and who will exist after this day. I love them and they love me. They advise one another and exchange gifts. They walk in the light of Allah among the people, gently, in secrecy and piety. They greet people, and people greet them, by their patience and forbearance. Their hearts return to the remembrance of Allah, and their mosques are full of their prayers. They show mercy to their young and honour their elders, and they share with one another. Their wealthy give to their poor, and their strong to their weak. They visit their sick and follow their funerals."

A man from the people said: "Do they show kindness to their companions in that?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned to him and said: "No indeed. They have no companions; they serve themselves. They are too honourable before Allah for Him to expand provision upon them, because of the baseness of this world in the sight of their Lord." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾

It is reported that al-Hasan, when he recited these two verses, said: "This describes their days."

Then He said: ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord prostrating and standing﴾. This describes their nights.

Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever prays two rak'ahs or more at night has spent the night before Allah, the Exalted, prostrating and standing.

Al-Kalbi said: it is said: two rak'ahs after maghrib and four after 'isha' (the last prayer).

﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed its punishment is ever adhering﴾, meaning constant, perpetual, inseparable, for those disbelievers who are punished by it. From this comes the word *gharim* (creditor), because he demands his right, insists upon it from his debtor, and clings to him. One says: "So-and-so is *mughram* with so-and-so" when he is fond of him, cannot bear to be without him, and does not part from him. Al-A'sha said:

*If he punishes, it will be a constant torment; and if he gives abundantly, he does not care.*

Al-Hasan said: "They know that every creditor parts from his debtor except the creditor of Hell" [[In the second copy an addition: Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, asked the disbelievers for the price of His blessings, and they did not pay it. So He made them debtors and admitted them to the Fire.]].

Ibn Zayd said: *gharam* is evil. Abu 'Ubayd said: destruction. Bishr ibn Abi Hazim said:

*And the day of al-Nisar and the day of al-Jifar were a punishment, and they were a torment,*

meaning destruction.

﴿Indeed it is, meaning Hell, evil as a settlement and residence﴾, meaning a dwelling, from *aqama, yuqimu*.

Salamah ibn Jandal said:

*Two days: a day of stations and gatherings, and a day of travelling to the enemies, returning.*

If the *mim* is vowelled with a fatha, it means the place of standing, from *qama, yaqumu*, and from it is the saying of 'Abbas ibn Mirdas:

*So as for your deed, it was evil; therefore, you are bound to the station, and will not see it.*

﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾. The readers differed concerning it. The people of Medina and Syria recited *yuqtiru* with a damma on the *ya'* and a kasra on the *ta'*. The people of Kufa recited with a fatha on the *ya'* and a damma on the *ta'*. Others recited with a fatha on the *ya'* and a kasra on the *ta'*. All are valid dialects. It is said: *aqtara* and *qatara, yaqturu* and *yaqtiru*, like *ya'rishuna* and *ya'kifuna*.

The commentators differed about the meaning of *israf* (extravagance) and *iqtar* (stinginess). Some said: *israf* is spending in disobedience to Allah, even if little; and *iqtar* is withholding the right of Allah, the Exalted. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Ishaq al-Kulawadhi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath [in the second copy an addition: ibn Harun ibn Sulayman al-Ash'ath] narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm narrated to us, from Kathir ibn Ziyad Abu Sahl, from al-Hasan, concerning this verse, that he said: "They did not spend in the disobedience of Allah, and they did not withhold from the obligations of Allah."

Others said: *israf* is that you eat the wealth of another without right.

'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah said: "The extravagant is not one who eats his own wealth; the extravagant is one who eats the wealth of another."

Others said: *sarf* is exceeding the limit in spending, and *iqtar* is falling short of what is due in what is necessary. This is the chosen view, because of His word: ﴿And was between that﴾, meaning their spending was between those two, ﴿a standard﴾, meaning just, moderate, middle between extravagance and stinginess.

Ibrahim said: "He does not starve them, nor leave them naked, nor spend in a way that people say, 'He has been extravagant.'"

Muqatil said: "They earned what was good, spent with moderation, and sent forward surplus, so they profited and succeeded."

Yazid ibn Abi Habib said concerning this verse: "Those were the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). They did not eat food for luxury and pleasure, nor wear clothing for beauty. Rather, they sought from food only what would relieve their hunger and strengthen them to worship their Lord, and from clothing only what would cover their nakedness and shield them from heat and cold."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Abu 'Uyaynah, from a man, from al-Hasan, concerning the word of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿they were neither extravagant nor stingy﴾: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'It is enough extravagance that a man desires something and buys it and eats it.'"

﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ ... the verse.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 25, verses 53–77 (part 2 of 3):

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhaldi informed us, saying: al-Mu'ammal ibn al-Hasan ibn Isa informed us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us from Abu Jurayj, who said: Ya'la, that is Ibn Muslim, informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he heard him narrate from Ibn Abbas that some people of the polytheists had killed many and committed fornication many times, then they came to Muhammad (ﷺ) and said: "What you say and call to is indeed good; if only you would tell us that there is an expiation for what we have done." So there was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾, and there was revealed: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ [[Surah al-Zumar: 53.]]. It was also said: it was revealed concerning Wahshi, the freedman of Ibn Mut'im.

And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar and al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur and al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il.

And Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan and Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Yusuf ibn Abdullah ibn Mahan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn al-A'mash, Mansur and Wasil al-Ahdab narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il.

And Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Makki ibn Abdan informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from Shaqiq, from Amr ibn Shurahbil, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child for fear that it will eat with you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed in confirmation of that: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ [[Sahih reference omitted in source.]] [88].

Musafi' said: ﴿And they do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and they do not commit adultery﴾, the verse...

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hanash narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh informed us, saying: Salama ibn Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that Luqman used to say: "O my son, beware of fornication, for its beginning is fear and its end is regret." ﴿And whoever does that which you have mentioned shall meet a penalty﴾ [Ibn Abbas said: "A sin (athaman), and its metaphorical sense is: he will meet the recompense of sins."]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hafsawayh narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: al-Kalbi narrated to us, saying: Sharqi al-Qitami narrated to us, saying: Luqman ibn Amir narrated to me, saying: Abu Umama al-Bahili, Sadi ibn Ajlan, narrated to me. I said: "Narrate to me a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He then called for a drink, and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "If a rock of ten 'ashrawat' weight were thrown into the brink of Hell, it would not reach its bottom in seventy autumns; then it would reach Ghayy and Athām." I said: "And what are Ghayy and Athām?" He said: "Fires in which the pus of the people of the Fire flows; and they are the two of which Allah, exalted is He, said in His Book: ﴿So they will meet Ghayy﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 59.]] and ﴿shall meet Athām﴾ [[Musnad al-Shamiyyin, al-Tabarani: 2/405.]].

And Abu Amr Sa'id ibn Abdullah ibn Isma'il al-Hiri informed us, saying: al-Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Qawhabad informed us, saying: Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Zarin al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Abd al-Rahman informed us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from Abu Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, that Athām is a valley in Hell; and this is the saying of Mujahid. Abu Ubayd said: al-Athām: the punishment.

Al-Laythi said:
"May Allah reward Ibn Urwa, since he has become
an act of disobedience, and disobedience for him is athām."
That is, a punishment.

﴿His punishment will be doubled on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾ The common readers recite it with jazm on the fa' and the dal, while Ibn Amir and Ibn Abbas read them with raf' as a new beginning (ibtida').

Then He said: ﴿Except one who repents and believes and does righteous work﴾, the verse...

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Harun al-Jammal narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Shafi'i narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Raja narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "We recited it in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for years [In the second copy: two years]: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾, the verse. Then there was revealed: ﴿except one who repents,﴾ and I never saw the Prophet (ﷺ) rejoice at anything as he rejoiced at it, and at ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what follows﴾."

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Fanjawi informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Yaqtini narrated to us, saying:
Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Uqayli informed us, saying: Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: al-Qasim ibn Abi Burra narrated to me, who said:
I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Abu Abdullah, what do you say about the words of Allah, exalted and majestic: ﴿And they do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾ up to His words ﴿except one who repents﴾?" He said: "I heard Ibn Abbas say: this is a Meccan verse, abrogated by the Medinan verse in Surah al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein, and there is no repentance for him.﴾"

Abu al-Zinad narrated from Kharija ibn Zayd ibn Thabit that he entered upon his father while with him was a man from the people of Iraq, asking him about this verse in al-Furqan and the verse in Surah al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 93.]]. Zayd ibn Thabit said: "You have known the abrogating from the abrogated; its abrogating verse in al-Nisa' came six months later."

Hajjaj narrated from Abu Jurayj, who said: al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: "Between this surah and al-Nisa' [and the verse] ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ are eight years." But the correct view is that it is muhkam (not abrogated).

Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated from Amr ibn Malik al-Bakri, from Abu al-Jawza', who said: "I frequented Ibn Abbas for thirteen years, and whenever there was any verse of the Qur'an I asked him about it. My messenger frequented Aisha. I never heard him, nor any of the scholars, say that Allah, exalted is He, says of a sin: 'I will not forgive it.'"

﴿Those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: that is, Allah will replace for them the ugly deeds of their polytheism with the fine deeds of Islam; He will replace shirk with faith, the killing of believers with the killing of polytheists, and fornication with chastity and marriage. Others said: that is, Allah will replace their evil deeds which they committed while in Islam with good deeds on the Day of Resurrection. What supports this interpretation is what

Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Hafiz informed me in my house, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Barzah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hafs al-Mustamli narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz Abi Rizma narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa al-Qati'i narrated to us, from Abu al-Anbas, from his son, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Some people will surely wish that they had multiplied their evil deeds." It was said: "Who are they?" He said: "Those whose evil deeds Allah has replaced with good deeds." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/78.]] [89].

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: 'Present to him his minor sins.' His minor sins will be presented to him, and his major sins will be concealed from him, and it will be said: 'You did on such and such a day such and such, and such and such.' He will acknowledge it and not deny it, while he is apprehensive about the major sins. It will then be said: 'Give him, in place of every evil deed he did, a good deed.' He will say: 'Indeed I have sins which I do not see here.' I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laugh until his molars showed." [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/157.]] [90].

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Samura al-Baghawi in Baghdad, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Taliqani narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Harun Abu Nashit narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from Abu al-Tawil Shatb al-Mamdud, that he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who committed all sins and left none of them, and in that he did not leave any need (hajah) or any road-cutting (dajah) without seizing it with his right hand? Is there repentance for such a one?"
He said: "Have you embraced Islam?"
He said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and that you are His Messenger." He said: "Yes; you will do good deeds and abandon desires, and Allah will make them all good deeds."
He said: "And my betrayals and my debaucheries?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Allah is greater," and he kept saying "Allah is greater" until he disappeared. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/78.]] [91].

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me in a group, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nashit narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: I heard Mubashshir ibn Ubayd, who was knowledgeable in grammar and Arabic, say: "The hajah is the one who cuts off the pilgrims when they set out, and the dajah is the one who cuts them off when they return." ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work, indeed he turns to Allah with a good turning (mataban)﴾, i.e., a good return.

﴿And those who do not bear witness to falsehood (al-zur)﴾. Al-Dahhak said: it means shirk and the exaltation of rivals. Ali ibn Abi Talha said: it means false testimony; Umar ibn al-Khattab used to flog a false witness forty lashes, blacken his face, and parade him in the market. Yahya ibn al-Yaman, from Mujahid: the festivals of the polytheists. Layth, from him: singing; and this is the saying of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya. With an isnad through al-Salihi, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: "It has reached me that Allah, exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'Where are those who used to keep themselves and their ears pure from idle amusement and the flutes of Satan? Admit them into the gardens of musk. Let My servants hear My praise, My thanks, and My glorification, and inform them that ﴿no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾.'"

Abu Bakr al-Juzqani informed us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad al-Ar'yani narrated to us, saying: al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Amr al-Abqari narrated to us, saying: Maslama ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Amr ibn Qays concerning His words, exalted is He: ﴿who do not bear witness to falsehood﴾: "gatherings of obscenity." Ibn Jurayj: lying. Qatada: gatherings of falsehood. The root of zur is to beautify a thing and describe it contrary to its reality, until the one who hears or sees it imagines it to be other than it is; it is the embellishment of falsehood in what is supposed to be truth.

﴿And when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity (kiraman)﴾. Muqatil said: when they hear from the disbelievers abuse and harm, they turn away and forgive; this is the narration of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid. Its parallel is ﴿and when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 55.]], the verse... Al-Suddi said: it is abrogated by the verse of fighting. Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Mujahid: when they come upon mention of marriage, they allude to it indirectly. Ibn Zayd: when they pass by what the polytheists engaged in of falsehood, they pass by denying it and turning away from it. Al-Hasan and al-Kalbi said: al-laghw (idle talk) is all acts of disobedience; that is, when they pass by gatherings of amusement and falsehood, they pass by kiraman, hastening and turning away. This is supported by what

Ibrahim ibn Maysara narrated: that Ibn Mas'ud passed by a place of amusement, hastening, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Ibn Mas'ud is noble (la-kariman)." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 19/64.]] [92].

And the people of language said: its origin is from the saying of the Arabs: a noble she-camel (naqah karimah), a noble cow, a noble ewe, when she turns away from being milked, showing nobility, as if she does not care about what is milked from her.

﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind (lam yakhirru)﴾: they did not fall or collapse upon them, "deaf and blind," as if they were deaf and blind; rather they hear what they are reminded of, understand it, see the truth in it, and follow it.

Al-Farra' said: the meaning of His words lam yakhirru is: they did not remain or become; the Arabs say: "I cursed so-and-so, and he stood weeping," meaning he remained and began weeping, and there was no standing there; perhaps he wept while seated. "So-and-so sat reviling me," meaning he began and went on reviling me. This is permissible in the speech of the Arabs.

﴿And those who say: "Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and our offspring the coolness of our eyes"﴾: Abu Amr and the people of Kufa read dhurriyyatina without alif; the rest read dhurriyyatina with alif. Qurrata a'yun: that He show them to be believing, righteous, and obedient to You. He made qurrah singular because it is a verbal noun (masdar); its origin is from coolness, because the Arabs are harmed by heat and find rest in coolness.

﴿And make us leaders (imaman) for the God-fearing﴾: that is, examples (a'imma) to be followed. Ibn Abbas said: make us leaders of guidance, as He said: ﴿and We made them leaders guiding by Our command﴾ [[Surah al-Anbiya': 73.]], and do not make us leaders of misguidance, as He said: ﴿and We made them leaders calling to the Fire﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 41.]]. Qatada: guides and callers to good.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Faqih informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Azi al-Tabari, known as Ibn Fayruz, narrated to me, saying: al-Hakam ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hamza narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Jabir, from Makhul, concerning the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿and make us leaders for the God-fearing﴾, he said: "Leaders in piety, to be followed by the God-fearing." Some of them said: this is inverted (min al-maqlub): "make the God-fearing leaders for us, and make us followers (mu'tammin) and imitators (muqtadin) of them." This is the saying of Mujahid. It was not said a'imma (plural) because imam is a verbal noun; one says amma fulan fulanan, like siyam and qiyam. Whoever makes it plural does so because it has become so common that it has come to function as an adjective.

Some of them said: he meant a'imma in the sense of how a speaker says "our amir, these": meaning our amirs (umara'). Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿for they are an enemy to me﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara': 77.]], and a poet said:
"O my blamers, do not increase your reproach,
for the blamers are not trustworthy to me."
That is, amina' (trustworthy).

﴿Those will be rewarded with the lofty chamber (al-ghurfa)﴾: they will be given the high rank in Paradise, "for what they endured" in obedience to their Lord's command and their Prophet's guidance.

Al-Baqir said: "for patience in poverty."

﴿And they will be met with greeting and peace (yulaqqawna)﴾: the people of Kufa read it with a fatha on the ya' and light qaf, and this is what al-Farra' chose, saying: because the Arabs say "fulan yalqa bil-salam" and "bil-khabar" with the ba', and rarely say "yalqa al-salam"; the others read yulaqqawna with shadda, and this is what Abu Ubayd chose, because of His words: ﴿and He gave them radiance and joy﴾ [[Surah al-Insan: 11.]].

﴿Abiding therein; how good it is as a place of rest and dwelling.﴾

﴿Say: "My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication"﴾: ya'bA'u bikum: that is, what He would do or make of you, according to Mujahid and Ibn Zayd. Abu Ubayd said: one says "ma 'abe'tu bihi shay'an," meaning I did not reckon it, so its existence and non-existence are the same; its meaning is: what measure do you have? The root of this word is preparing a thing; one says "'abba'tu al-jaysh" and "'abba'tu al-tib a'abbi'uhu 'abwan wa 'abwan," when I prepared and made it ready. The poet said:
"As if upon his neck and his shoulders
was perfume that a bride had prepared for him overnight."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 1/118.]] ﴿Were it not for your supplication﴾: and it was said: were it not for your worship; and it was said: were it not for your faith. The scholars differed concerning the meaning of this verse. One group said: its meaning is, "Say: My Lord would not care for your creation were it not for your worship and obedience to Him," meaning He created you for His worship, like His words: ﴿And I did not create jinn and humankind except that they may worship Me﴾ [[Surah al-Dhariyat: 56.]]; this is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. Ibn Abbas, in the narration of al-Walibi, said: Allah informed the disbelievers that their Lord has no need of them, since He did not create them as believers; had He had need of them, He would have made faith beloved to them as He made it beloved to the believers.

Others said: "Say: My Lord would not care for your punishment were it not for your calling upon Him in hardships," as in His words: ﴿And when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [[Surah al-Ankabut: 65.]] and similar verses.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 25, verse 53–77 (part 3 of 3):

Some of them said: ﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you were it not for your calling upon Him.﴾ Its explanation is His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 147.]] This meaning is the saying of al-Dahhak.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Abu Hatim narrated to us, saying: Abu Tahir ibn al-Sarj narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Rabi'a al-Jumahi narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Walid ibn al-Walid say: It has reached me that the tafsir of this verse, ﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you were it not for your calling upon Him,﴾ is: "I did not create you while I have any need of you, except that you ask Me, and I forgive you, and you ask Me, and I give you."

﴿Then you have indeed denied,﴾ O people of Makkah.

Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Makki ibn Abdan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba ibn Abd al-Hamid ibn Wasil narrated to us, saying: I heard Muslim ibn Ammar say: I heard Ibn Abbas recite: ﴿Then the disbelievers have indeed denied, so it will be inevitable (lizaman).﴾

And with this chain, Shu'ba narrated from Adham, meaning al-Sadusi, that Khalaf ibn al-Zubayr used to recite ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾, and when he reached this verse he recited it: ﴿Then the disbeliever has indeed denied, so it will be inevitable (lizaman).﴾ The meaning of the verse is: "so their denial will be inevitable (lizaman)." Ibn Abbas said: death. Ibn Zayd: fighting. Abu Ubayda: destruction.

And he recited:

"So if they escape the death of my land, they have met their deaths inevitably (lizaman)."

[[Lisan al-Arab: 12/541.]]

Some of the people of meanings said: it means that there will be a recompense which binds every doer to what he has done, whether good or evil. Ibn Jarir said: it means lasting, binding punishment and an annihilating destruction that overtakes some of you after others, like the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb:

"So it struck him with a sudden hostile blow, inevitable, as the basin pours forth the pebbly ground."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 19/71.]]

He means by "lizam" the abundant, which follows one another, and by "lafif" the stones that are piled up. They differed about the meaning of "lizam" here. A group said: it is the Day of Badr, when seventy of them were killed and seventy taken prisoner; this is the saying of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Malik, Mujahid and Muqatil.

Al-A'mash narrated from Muslim, from Masruq, who said: Abdullah said: "Five have passed: the smoke, the lizam, the assault, the moon, and the Romans."

Others said: it is the punishment of the Hereafter.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 25, verses 53–77 (part 1 of 3)**

﴿And He it is who released the two seas﴾, meaning He mixed them, let them meet, and let one flow into the other. The root of *maraj* (mixing and letting loose) is *al-khalt wa'l-irsal*, and from it comes His saying ﴿So they are in a confused matter﴾ [[Surah Qaf: 5.]].

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar: "How will you be, O 'Abd Allah, when you are among a worthless remnant of people whose covenants and trusts have been confused and who have become like this?" [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 15/125.]] [86] And he interlaced his fingers.

It is said: *maragat dabbati marjaha*, meaning I let my beast loose to graze and left it to go wherever it wished. From this comes the word *marj* for a meadow. Al-'Ajjaj said:

*Grazing in it was a spring meadow, varied in colour.*

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: ﴿released the two seas﴾ means one of them was spread over the other. ﴿This one is sweet, fresh and pleasant﴾, meaning exceedingly sweet, ﴿and this one is salt, bitter and briny﴾, meaning exceedingly salty. ﴿And He placed between them a barrier﴾, a partition by His power and wisdom, ﴿and a forbidding ban﴾, a protective screen that prevents them, ﴿so that they do not transgress﴾, and the sweet water is not corrupted by the salt.

﴿And He it is who created from water a human being and made him [a line of] descent and marriage relation﴾.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: *nasab* is that whose marriage is forbidden, and *sihr* is that whose marriage is permitted. Al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Muqatil said: *nasab* is seven and *sihr* is five, and they recited this verse: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters﴾ to its end.

Abu 'Abd Allah [al-Qasayni] informed me, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Nasibi, the judge, informed us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Subay'i al-Halabi informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas al-Miqana'i narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Husayn al-Ashqar narrated to us, saying: Abu Qutaybah al-Taymi narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Sirin say, concerning the word of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿And He it is who created from water a human being and made him [a line of] descent and marriage relation﴾: "It was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, the husband of Fatimah. He was his paternal cousin and the husband of his daughter, so it was [both] descent and marriage relation" [[Nazm Durar al-Simtayn, al-Zarandi al-Hanafi: p. 92.]].

﴿And your Lord is ever Competent﴾. ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which neither benefits them﴾ if they worship it, ﴿nor harms them﴾ if they abandon it. ﴿And the disbeliever is ever a helper [of Satan] against his Lord﴾, meaning an aide to Satan against his Lord. It is also said that the meaning is: the disbeliever is despised and humiliated before his Lord, from the Arab expression *zahirtu bihi* when you put someone behind your back and do not turn towards him.

﴿And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾. ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any payment for it﴾, meaning for conveying the revelation. They would say: "Muhammad only seeks our wealth by what he calls us to, so we will not follow him, lest we give him any of our wealth." ﴿Except for him who wills to take to his Lord a way﴾.

The scholars of meaning (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: this is a disjunctive exception (*istithna' munqati'*), its sense being: "but whoever wills to take to his Lord a way," by spending his wealth in the way of Allah.

﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt Him with His praise﴾, meaning worship Him and pray to Him, thanking Him for His blessings. It is also said: praise Him, declaring Him free of what is impermissible in His attributes. It is also said: say, "Subhan Allah and al-hamdu lillah." ﴿And sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants﴾, so that He will recompense them for them.

﴿Who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾. He said "between them" though He mentioned the heavens (in plural), because He meant the two kinds and the two things, like the words of al-Qutami:

*Has it not grieved you that the ropes of Qays and Taghlib have been severed in separation?*

He meant "the ropes of Taghlib," so he used the dual, while *hibal* is a plural, because he meant two things and two types. Another said:

*Indeed death and its calamities, both of them, make the mountain passes and my lands their target.*

﴿Then He established Himself above the Throne, the Most Merciful﴾. ﴿So ask about Him one well-informed﴾, meaning: ask one informed about the Most Merciful. It is also said: ask about Him an expert, and he is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is also said: he is Jibril (peace be upon him). The *ba'* here means *'an* (about), following the saying of the poet:

*If you ask me about women, indeed I am an expert in the ailments of women, a physician.*

meaning: about women.

﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command us?"﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited *ya'muruna* with a *ya'* (meaning: to what they command us), while others recited *ta'muruna* with a *ta'* (meaning: to what you command us, O Muhammad). ﴿And it increased them in aversion﴾, meaning the saying of the one who said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," increased them in aversion from the religion and faith. Sufyan al-Thawri, when he recited this verse, would raise his head to the sky and say: "My God, You have increased me in humility; may Your enemies' aversion not increase."

﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾, meaning the stations of the seven wandering planets. They are twelve constellations: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces. Aries and Scorpio are the houses of Mars; Taurus and Libra are the houses of Venus; Gemini and Virgo are the houses of Mercury; Cancer is the house of the Moon; Leo is the house of the Sun; Sagittarius and Pisces are the houses of Jupiter; Capricorn and Aquarius are the houses of Saturn. These constellations are divided among the four elements, so each of them has three constellations called the *muthallathat* (triplicities). Aries, Leo and Sagittarius are the fiery triplicity; Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn are the earthy triplicity; Gemini, Libra and Aquarius are the airy triplicity; Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces are the watery triplicity. The opinions of the commentators differ regarding the interpretation of *burudj* (constellations).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Shaykh narrated to me, saying: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from 'Ata' al-'Awfi, concerning the word of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾, that he said: "Palaces in which there are guards." Its evidence is His word: ﴿And even if you were in towers well-built﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 78.]].

Al-Akhtal said:

*As if it were a Roman tower, built by a builder with plaster, bricks and stones.*

Mujahid and Qatadah said: they are the stars.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Mahan narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, saying: my maternal uncle Ya'la narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, concerning ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾, that he said: "The great stars." 'Ata' said: they are the *sharaj*, which are the gates of the sky, called the Milky Way.

﴿And placed therein a lamp﴾, meaning the sun, similar to His word: ﴿And made the sun a lamp﴾ [[Surah Nuh: 16.]]. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited (*wa-ja'ala fiha suruja*) in the plural, meaning the stars, and this is the reading of the companions of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud). ﴿And a moon giving light﴾.

﴿And He it is who made the night and the day in succession﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning a replacement and a successor, one standing in place of the other, so whoever misses his deed in one of them makes it up in the other.

Qatadah said: "Show Allah good deeds in this night and day, for they are two steeds that carry people to their terms, that bring near everything far away, that wear out everything new, and that bring every promised thing to the Day of Resurrection."

Shamir [in the second copy: Shams] ibn 'Atiyyah narrated from Shaqiq, who said: A man came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "I missed the prayer last night." He said: "Make up what you missed of your night in your day, for Allah, the Exalted, made the night and the day in succession for whoever wishes to take heed."

Mujahid said: meaning He made each of them contrary to the other: this one black and that one white.

Ibn Zayd and others said: meaning one succeeds the other; when one goes, the other comes. They alternate in light and darkness, in increase and decrease. The following verse of Zuhayr supports this interpretation:

*In them the gazelles and the cows walk in succession, and their young ones rise from every bent-legged one.*

Muqatil said: meaning He made the day a successor to the night for whoever sleeps at night, and made the night a successor to the day for whoever has a need or is occupied.

﴿For whoever wishes to take heed﴾. The common readers recite it with a doubled *dhal*, meaning he remembers and admonishes himself. Hamzah and Khalaf recite it with a single *dhal*, from *dhikr* (remembrance). ﴿Or wishes gratitude﴾, meaning gratitude for the blessing of Allah, the Exalted, upon him.

﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful﴾, meaning the excellent servants. It is said this idiom (of *'ibad*) is for specification and distinction. Al-Hasan recited: *wa-'ubayd al-Rahman*.

﴿Those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾, meaning with tranquillity, dignity, obedience and humility, not arrogant, not exultant, not haughty, and not corrupters.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Qawhar informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi 'Isa narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Hushaym ibn 'Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His word, the Exalted, ﴿walk upon the earth in humility﴾, that he said: "Forbearance and knowledge." Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "They are people of dignity and chastity who do not behave foolishly; and if foolishness is directed at them, they show forbearance."

Al-Dahhak said: "Pious and chaste people who do not act ignorantly." He said: and it is in Syriac. Al-Thumali said: it is in Nabataean. The word *hawn* in the language means gentleness and softness, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Love your beloved gently, for he may one day become your enemy; and hate your enemy gently, for he may one day become your beloved." [[Al-Musannaf, al-San'ani: 11/181.]].

﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"﴾, meaning words of soundness, from Mujahid.

Ibn Hayyan said: words by which they are safe from sin.

Al-Hasan said: they greet them with peace. Its evidence is His word: ﴿And when they hear vain speech, they turn away from it and say, "To us are our deeds and to you are your deeds; peace be upon you"﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 55.]].

Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Kalbi said: this was before they were commanded to fight; then the verse of fighting abrogated it.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash, the reciter, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih [al-Kaylisi] [[So in the manuscript.]] narrated to us in Makkah, saying: Salamah ibn Shabib [in the second copy: Shu'ayb] narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Shaybān ibn Mihran narrated to us, from Khalid ibn al-Mughirah ibn Qays, from Abu Mihlaz Lahiq ibn Humayd, from Abu Barzah al-Aslami, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "I have seen people from my community who have not yet been created, and who will exist after this day. I love them and they love me. They advise one another and exchange gifts. They walk in the light of Allah among the people, gently, in secrecy and piety. They greet people, and people greet them, by their patience and forbearance. Their hearts return to the remembrance of Allah, and their mosques are full of their prayers. They show mercy to their young and honour their elders, and they share with one another. Their wealthy give to their poor, and their strong to their weak. They visit their sick and follow their funerals."

A man from the people said: "Do they show kindness to their companions in that?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned to him and said: "No indeed. They have no companions; they serve themselves. They are too honourable before Allah for Him to expand provision upon them, because of the baseness of this world in the sight of their Lord." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾

It is reported that al-Hasan, when he recited these two verses, said: "This describes their days."

Then He said: ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord prostrating and standing﴾. This describes their nights.

Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever prays two rak'ahs or more at night has spent the night before Allah, the Exalted, prostrating and standing.

Al-Kalbi said: it is said: two rak'ahs after maghrib and four after 'isha' (the last prayer).

﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed its punishment is ever adhering﴾, meaning constant, perpetual, inseparable, for those disbelievers who are punished by it. From this comes the word *gharim* (creditor), because he demands his right, insists upon it from his debtor, and clings to him. One says: "So-and-so is *mughram* with so-and-so" when he is fond of him, cannot bear to be without him, and does not part from him. Al-A'sha said:

*If he punishes, it will be a constant torment; and if he gives abundantly, he does not care.*

Al-Hasan said: "They know that every creditor parts from his debtor except the creditor of Hell" [[In the second copy an addition: Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, asked the disbelievers for the price of His blessings, and they did not pay it. So He made them debtors and admitted them to the Fire.]].

Ibn Zayd said: *gharam* is evil. Abu 'Ubayd said: destruction. Bishr ibn Abi Hazim said:

*And the day of al-Nisar and the day of al-Jifar were a punishment, and they were a torment,*

meaning destruction.

﴿Indeed it is, meaning Hell, evil as a settlement and residence﴾, meaning a dwelling, from *aqama, yuqimu*.

Salamah ibn Jandal said:

*Two days: a day of stations and gatherings, and a day of travelling to the enemies, returning.*

If the *mim* is vowelled with a fatha, it means the place of standing, from *qama, yaqumu*, and from it is the saying of 'Abbas ibn Mirdas:

*So as for your deed, it was evil; therefore, you are bound to the station, and will not see it.*

﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾. The readers differed concerning it. The people of Medina and Syria recited *yuqtiru* with a damma on the *ya'* and a kasra on the *ta'*. The people of Kufa recited with a fatha on the *ya'* and a damma on the *ta'*. Others recited with a fatha on the *ya'* and a kasra on the *ta'*. All are valid dialects. It is said: *aqtara* and *qatara, yaqturu* and *yaqtiru*, like *ya'rishuna* and *ya'kifuna*.

The commentators differed about the meaning of *israf* (extravagance) and *iqtar* (stinginess). Some said: *israf* is spending in disobedience to Allah, even if little; and *iqtar* is withholding the right of Allah, the Exalted. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Ishaq al-Kulawadhi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath [in the second copy an addition: ibn Harun ibn Sulayman al-Ash'ath] narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm narrated to us, from Kathir ibn Ziyad Abu Sahl, from al-Hasan, concerning this verse, that he said: "They did not spend in the disobedience of Allah, and they did not withhold from the obligations of Allah."

Others said: *israf* is that you eat the wealth of another without right.

'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah said: "The extravagant is not one who eats his own wealth; the extravagant is one who eats the wealth of another."

Others said: *sarf* is exceeding the limit in spending, and *iqtar* is falling short of what is due in what is necessary. This is the chosen view, because of His word: ﴿And was between that﴾, meaning their spending was between those two, ﴿a standard﴾, meaning just, moderate, middle between extravagance and stinginess.

Ibrahim said: "He does not starve them, nor leave them naked, nor spend in a way that people say, 'He has been extravagant.'"

Muqatil said: "They earned what was good, spent with moderation, and sent forward surplus, so they profited and succeeded."

Yazid ibn Abi Habib said concerning this verse: "Those were the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). They did not eat food for luxury and pleasure, nor wear clothing for beauty. Rather, they sought from food only what would relieve their hunger and strengthen them to worship their Lord, and from clothing only what would cover their nakedness and shield them from heat and cold."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Abu 'Uyaynah, from a man, from al-Hasan, concerning the word of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿they were neither extravagant nor stingy﴾: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'It is enough extravagance that a man desires something and buys it and eats it.'"

﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ ... the verse.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 25, verses 53–77 (part 2 of 3):

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhaldi informed us, saying: al-Mu'ammal ibn al-Hasan ibn Isa informed us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us from Abu Jurayj, who said: Ya'la, that is Ibn Muslim, informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he heard him narrate from Ibn Abbas that some people of the polytheists had killed many and committed fornication many times, then they came to Muhammad (ﷺ) and said: "What you say and call to is indeed good; if only you would tell us that there is an expiation for what we have done." So there was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾, and there was revealed: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ [[Surah al-Zumar: 53.]]. It was also said: it was revealed concerning Wahshi, the freedman of Ibn Mut'im.

And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar and al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur and al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il.

And Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan and Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Yusuf ibn Abdullah ibn Mahan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn al-A'mash, Mansur and Wasil al-Ahdab narrated to us, from Abu Wa'il.

And Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, saying: Makki ibn Abdan informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from Shaqiq, from Amr ibn Shurahbil, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child for fear that it will eat with you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed in confirmation of that: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ [[Sahih reference omitted in source.]] [88].

Musafi' said: ﴿And they do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and they do not commit adultery﴾, the verse...

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hanash narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zanjawayh informed us, saying: Salama ibn Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that Luqman used to say: "O my son, beware of fornication, for its beginning is fear and its end is regret." ﴿And whoever does that which you have mentioned shall meet a penalty﴾ [Ibn Abbas said: "A sin (athaman), and its metaphorical sense is: he will meet the recompense of sins."]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hafsawayh narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: al-Kalbi narrated to us, saying: Sharqi al-Qitami narrated to us, saying: Luqman ibn Amir narrated to me, saying: Abu Umama al-Bahili, Sadi ibn Ajlan, narrated to me. I said: "Narrate to me a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He then called for a drink, and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "If a rock of ten 'ashrawat' weight were thrown into the brink of Hell, it would not reach its bottom in seventy autumns; then it would reach Ghayy and Athām." I said: "And what are Ghayy and Athām?" He said: "Fires in which the pus of the people of the Fire flows; and they are the two of which Allah, exalted is He, said in His Book: ﴿So they will meet Ghayy﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 59.]] and ﴿shall meet Athām﴾ [[Musnad al-Shamiyyin, al-Tabarani: 2/405.]].

And Abu Amr Sa'id ibn Abdullah ibn Isma'il al-Hiri informed us, saying: al-Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Qawhabad informed us, saying: Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Zarin al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Abd al-Rahman informed us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from Abu Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, that Athām is a valley in Hell; and this is the saying of Mujahid. Abu Ubayd said: al-Athām: the punishment.

Al-Laythi said:
"May Allah reward Ibn Urwa, since he has become
an act of disobedience, and disobedience for him is athām."
That is, a punishment.

﴿His punishment will be doubled on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation.﴾ The common readers recite it with jazm on the fa' and the dal, while Ibn Amir and Ibn Abbas read them with raf' as a new beginning (ibtida').

Then He said: ﴿Except one who repents and believes and does righteous work﴾, the verse...

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Harun al-Jammal narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Shafi'i narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Raja narrated to us, from Ubaydullah ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "We recited it in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for years [In the second copy: two years]: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾, the verse. Then there was revealed: ﴿except one who repents,﴾ and I never saw the Prophet (ﷺ) rejoice at anything as he rejoiced at it, and at ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what follows﴾."

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Fanjawi informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Yaqtini narrated to us, saying:
Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Uqayli informed us, saying: Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: al-Qasim ibn Abi Burra narrated to me, who said:
I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Abu Abdullah, what do you say about the words of Allah, exalted and majestic: ﴿And they do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾ up to His words ﴿except one who repents﴾?" He said: "I heard Ibn Abbas say: this is a Meccan verse, abrogated by the Medinan verse in Surah al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein, and there is no repentance for him.﴾"

Abu al-Zinad narrated from Kharija ibn Zayd ibn Thabit that he entered upon his father while with him was a man from the people of Iraq, asking him about this verse in al-Furqan and the verse in Surah al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 93.]]. Zayd ibn Thabit said: "You have known the abrogating from the abrogated; its abrogating verse in al-Nisa' came six months later."

Hajjaj narrated from Abu Jurayj, who said: al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: "Between this surah and al-Nisa' [and the verse] ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ are eight years." But the correct view is that it is muhkam (not abrogated).

Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated from Amr ibn Malik al-Bakri, from Abu al-Jawza', who said: "I frequented Ibn Abbas for thirteen years, and whenever there was any verse of the Qur'an I asked him about it. My messenger frequented Aisha. I never heard him, nor any of the scholars, say that Allah, exalted is He, says of a sin: 'I will not forgive it.'"

﴿Those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: that is, Allah will replace for them the ugly deeds of their polytheism with the fine deeds of Islam; He will replace shirk with faith, the killing of believers with the killing of polytheists, and fornication with chastity and marriage. Others said: that is, Allah will replace their evil deeds which they committed while in Islam with good deeds on the Day of Resurrection. What supports this interpretation is what

Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Hafiz informed me in my house, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Barzah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hafs al-Mustamli narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz Abi Rizma narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa al-Qati'i narrated to us, from Abu al-Anbas, from his son, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Some people will surely wish that they had multiplied their evil deeds." It was said: "Who are they?" He said: "Those whose evil deeds Allah has replaced with good deeds." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/78.]] [89].

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: 'Present to him his minor sins.' His minor sins will be presented to him, and his major sins will be concealed from him, and it will be said: 'You did on such and such a day such and such, and such and such.' He will acknowledge it and not deny it, while he is apprehensive about the major sins. It will then be said: 'Give him, in place of every evil deed he did, a good deed.' He will say: 'Indeed I have sins which I do not see here.' I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laugh until his molars showed." [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/157.]] [90].

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Samura al-Baghawi in Baghdad, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Taliqani narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Harun Abu Nashit narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from Abu al-Tawil Shatb al-Mamdud, that he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who committed all sins and left none of them, and in that he did not leave any need (hajah) or any road-cutting (dajah) without seizing it with his right hand? Is there repentance for such a one?"
He said: "Have you embraced Islam?"
He said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner, and that you are His Messenger." He said: "Yes; you will do good deeds and abandon desires, and Allah will make them all good deeds."
He said: "And my betrayals and my debaucheries?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Allah is greater," and he kept saying "Allah is greater" until he disappeared. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 13/78.]] [91].

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me in a group, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nashit narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: I heard Mubashshir ibn Ubayd, who was knowledgeable in grammar and Arabic, say: "The hajah is the one who cuts off the pilgrims when they set out, and the dajah is the one who cuts them off when they return." ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work, indeed he turns to Allah with a good turning (mataban)﴾, i.e., a good return.

﴿And those who do not bear witness to falsehood (al-zur)﴾. Al-Dahhak said: it means shirk and the exaltation of rivals. Ali ibn Abi Talha said: it means false testimony; Umar ibn al-Khattab used to flog a false witness forty lashes, blacken his face, and parade him in the market. Yahya ibn al-Yaman, from Mujahid: the festivals of the polytheists. Layth, from him: singing; and this is the saying of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya. With an isnad through al-Salihi, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: "It has reached me that Allah, exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'Where are those who used to keep themselves and their ears pure from idle amusement and the flutes of Satan? Admit them into the gardens of musk. Let My servants hear My praise, My thanks, and My glorification, and inform them that ﴿no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾.'"

Abu Bakr al-Juzqani informed us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad al-Ar'yani narrated to us, saying: al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Amr al-Abqari narrated to us, saying: Maslama ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Amr ibn Qays concerning His words, exalted is He: ﴿who do not bear witness to falsehood﴾: "gatherings of obscenity." Ibn Jurayj: lying. Qatada: gatherings of falsehood. The root of zur is to beautify a thing and describe it contrary to its reality, until the one who hears or sees it imagines it to be other than it is; it is the embellishment of falsehood in what is supposed to be truth.

﴿And when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity (kiraman)﴾. Muqatil said: when they hear from the disbelievers abuse and harm, they turn away and forgive; this is the narration of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid. Its parallel is ﴿and when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 55.]], the verse... Al-Suddi said: it is abrogated by the verse of fighting. Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Mujahid: when they come upon mention of marriage, they allude to it indirectly. Ibn Zayd: when they pass by what the polytheists engaged in of falsehood, they pass by denying it and turning away from it. Al-Hasan and al-Kalbi said: al-laghw (idle talk) is all acts of disobedience; that is, when they pass by gatherings of amusement and falsehood, they pass by kiraman, hastening and turning away. This is supported by what

Ibrahim ibn Maysara narrated: that Ibn Mas'ud passed by a place of amusement, hastening, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Ibn Mas'ud is noble (la-kariman)." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 19/64.]] [92].

And the people of language said: its origin is from the saying of the Arabs: a noble she-camel (naqah karimah), a noble cow, a noble ewe, when she turns away from being milked, showing nobility, as if she does not care about what is milked from her.

﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind (lam yakhirru)﴾: they did not fall or collapse upon them, "deaf and blind," as if they were deaf and blind; rather they hear what they are reminded of, understand it, see the truth in it, and follow it.

Al-Farra' said: the meaning of His words lam yakhirru is: they did not remain or become; the Arabs say: "I cursed so-and-so, and he stood weeping," meaning he remained and began weeping, and there was no standing there; perhaps he wept while seated. "So-and-so sat reviling me," meaning he began and went on reviling me. This is permissible in the speech of the Arabs.

﴿And those who say: "Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and our offspring the coolness of our eyes"﴾: Abu Amr and the people of Kufa read dhurriyyatina without alif; the rest read dhurriyyatina with alif. Qurrata a'yun: that He show them to be believing, righteous, and obedient to You. He made qurrah singular because it is a verbal noun (masdar); its origin is from coolness, because the Arabs are harmed by heat and find rest in coolness.

﴿And make us leaders (imaman) for the God-fearing﴾: that is, examples (a'imma) to be followed. Ibn Abbas said: make us leaders of guidance, as He said: ﴿and We made them leaders guiding by Our command﴾ [[Surah al-Anbiya': 73.]], and do not make us leaders of misguidance, as He said: ﴿and We made them leaders calling to the Fire﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 41.]]. Qatada: guides and callers to good.

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Faqih informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Azi al-Tabari, known as Ibn Fayruz, narrated to me, saying: al-Hakam ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hamza narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Jabir, from Makhul, concerning the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿and make us leaders for the God-fearing﴾, he said: "Leaders in piety, to be followed by the God-fearing." Some of them said: this is inverted (min al-maqlub): "make the God-fearing leaders for us, and make us followers (mu'tammin) and imitators (muqtadin) of them." This is the saying of Mujahid. It was not said a'imma (plural) because imam is a verbal noun; one says amma fulan fulanan, like siyam and qiyam. Whoever makes it plural does so because it has become so common that it has come to function as an adjective.

Some of them said: he meant a'imma in the sense of how a speaker says "our amir, these": meaning our amirs (umara'). Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿for they are an enemy to me﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara': 77.]], and a poet said:
"O my blamers, do not increase your reproach,
for the blamers are not trustworthy to me."
That is, amina' (trustworthy).

﴿Those will be rewarded with the lofty chamber (al-ghurfa)﴾: they will be given the high rank in Paradise, "for what they endured" in obedience to their Lord's command and their Prophet's guidance.

Al-Baqir said: "for patience in poverty."

﴿And they will be met with greeting and peace (yulaqqawna)﴾: the people of Kufa read it with a fatha on the ya' and light qaf, and this is what al-Farra' chose, saying: because the Arabs say "fulan yalqa bil-salam" and "bil-khabar" with the ba', and rarely say "yalqa al-salam"; the others read yulaqqawna with shadda, and this is what Abu Ubayd chose, because of His words: ﴿and He gave them radiance and joy﴾ [[Surah al-Insan: 11.]].

﴿Abiding therein; how good it is as a place of rest and dwelling.﴾

﴿Say: "My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication"﴾: ya'bA'u bikum: that is, what He would do or make of you, according to Mujahid and Ibn Zayd. Abu Ubayd said: one says "ma 'abe'tu bihi shay'an," meaning I did not reckon it, so its existence and non-existence are the same; its meaning is: what measure do you have? The root of this word is preparing a thing; one says "'abba'tu al-jaysh" and "'abba'tu al-tib a'abbi'uhu 'abwan wa 'abwan," when I prepared and made it ready. The poet said:
"As if upon his neck and his shoulders
was perfume that a bride had prepared for him overnight."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 1/118.]] ﴿Were it not for your supplication﴾: and it was said: were it not for your worship; and it was said: were it not for your faith. The scholars differed concerning the meaning of this verse. One group said: its meaning is, "Say: My Lord would not care for your creation were it not for your worship and obedience to Him," meaning He created you for His worship, like His words: ﴿And I did not create jinn and humankind except that they may worship Me﴾ [[Surah al-Dhariyat: 56.]]; this is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. Ibn Abbas, in the narration of al-Walibi, said: Allah informed the disbelievers that their Lord has no need of them, since He did not create them as believers; had He had need of them, He would have made faith beloved to them as He made it beloved to the believers.

Others said: "Say: My Lord would not care for your punishment were it not for your calling upon Him in hardships," as in His words: ﴿And when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [[Surah al-Ankabut: 65.]] and similar verses.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 25, verse 53–77 (part 3 of 3):

Some of them said: ﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you were it not for your calling upon Him.﴾ Its explanation is His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 147.]] This meaning is the saying of al-Dahhak.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Abu Hatim narrated to us, saying: Abu Tahir ibn al-Sarj narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Rabi'a al-Jumahi narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Walid ibn al-Walid say: It has reached me that the tafsir of this verse, ﴿Say: My Lord would not care for you were it not for your calling upon Him,﴾ is: "I did not create you while I have any need of you, except that you ask Me, and I forgive you, and you ask Me, and I give you."

﴿Then you have indeed denied,﴾ O people of Makkah.

Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Makki ibn Abdan informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Azhar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba ibn Abd al-Hamid ibn Wasil narrated to us, saying: I heard Muslim ibn Ammar say: I heard Ibn Abbas recite: ﴿Then the disbelievers have indeed denied, so it will be inevitable (lizaman).﴾

And with this chain, Shu'ba narrated from Adham, meaning al-Sadusi, that Khalaf ibn al-Zubayr used to recite ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾, and when he reached this verse he recited it: ﴿Then the disbeliever has indeed denied, so it will be inevitable (lizaman).﴾ The meaning of the verse is: "so their denial will be inevitable (lizaman)." Ibn Abbas said: death. Ibn Zayd: fighting. Abu Ubayda: destruction.

And he recited:

"So if they escape the death of my land, they have met their deaths inevitably (lizaman)."

[[Lisan al-Arab: 12/541.]]

Some of the people of meanings said: it means that there will be a recompense which binds every doer to what he has done, whether good or evil. Ibn Jarir said: it means lasting, binding punishment and an annihilating destruction that overtakes some of you after others, like the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb:

"So it struck him with a sudden hostile blow, inevitable, as the basin pours forth the pebbly ground."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 19/71.]]

He means by "lizam" the abundant, which follows one another, and by "lafif" the stones that are piled up. They differed about the meaning of "lizam" here. A group said: it is the Day of Badr, when seventy of them were killed and seventy taken prisoner; this is the saying of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Malik, Mujahid and Muqatil.

Al-A'mash narrated from Muslim, from Masruq, who said: Abdullah said: "Five have passed: the smoke, the lizam, the assault, the moon, and the Romans."

Others said: it is the punishment of the Hereafter.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 25, verses 53–77 (part 1 of 3)**

﴿And He it is who released the two seas﴾, meaning He mixed them, let them meet, and let one flow into the other. The root of *maraj* (mixing and letting loose) is *al-khalt wa'l-irsal*, and from it comes His saying ﴿So they are in a confused matter﴾ [[Surah Qaf: 5.]].

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar: "How will you be, O 'Abd Allah, when you are among a worthless remnant of people whose covenants and trusts have been confused and who have become like this?" [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 15/125.]] [86] And he interlaced his fingers.

It is said: *maragat dabbati marjaha*, meaning I let my beast loose to graze and left it to go wherever it wished. From this comes the word *marj* for a meadow. Al-'Ajjaj said:

*Grazing in it was a spring meadow, varied in colour.*

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: ﴿released the two seas﴾ means one of them was spread over the other. ﴿This one is sweet, fresh and pleasant﴾, meaning exceedingly sweet, ﴿and this one is salt, bitter and briny﴾, meaning exceedingly salty. ﴿And He placed between them a barrier﴾, a partition by His power and wisdom, ﴿and a forbidding ban﴾, a protective screen that prevents them, ﴿so that they do not transgress﴾, and the sweet water is not corrupted by the salt.

﴿And He it is who created from water a human being and made him [a line of] descent and marriage relation﴾.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: *nasab* is that whose marriage is forbidden, and *sihr* is that whose marriage is permitted. Al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Muqatil said: *nasab* is seven and *sihr* is five, and they recited this verse: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters﴾ to its end.

Abu 'Abd Allah [al-Qasayni] informed me, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Nasibi, the judge, informed us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Subay'i al-Halabi informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas al-Miqana'i narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Husayn al-Ashqar narrated to us, saying: Abu Qutaybah al-Taymi narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Sirin say, concerning the word of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿And He it is who created from water a human being and made him [a line of] descent and marriage relation﴾: "It was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, the husband of Fatimah. He was his paternal cousin and the husband of his daughter, so it was [both] descent and marriage relation" [[Nazm Durar al-Simtayn, al-Zarandi al-Hanafi: p. 92.]].

﴿And your Lord is ever Competent﴾. ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which neither benefits them﴾ if they worship it, ﴿nor harms them﴾ if they abandon it. ﴿And the disbeliever is ever a helper [of Satan] against his Lord﴾, meaning an aide to Satan against his Lord. It is also said that the meaning is: the disbeliever is despised and humiliated before his Lord, from the Arab expression *zahirtu bihi* when you put someone behind your back and do not turn towards him.

﴿And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾. ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any payment for it﴾, meaning for conveying the revelation. They would say: "Muhammad only seeks our wealth by what he calls us to, so we will not follow him, lest we give him any of our wealth." ﴿Except for him who wills to take to his Lord a way﴾.

The scholars of meaning (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: this is a disjunctive exception (*istithna' munqati'*), its sense being: "but whoever wills to take to his Lord a way," by spending his wealth in the way of Allah.

﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt Him with His praise﴾, meaning worship Him and pray to Him, thanking Him for His blessings. It is also said: praise Him, declaring Him free of what is impermissible in His attributes.
